Houses an exhibition and presentation hall, the information centre and a 4-room hotel (1 single 40 GEL, 2 double 50 GEL, 1 lux 60 GEL) sleeping a maximum of 7; tents, sleeping bags, mats, backpacks, binoculars and fly-fishing gear are hired here. Contact: visitor service specialist Nino Seturidze, +995 577 10 18 49. Coordinate is ~13 km NW of the park polygon and west of the task bbox, which is expected: the administration sits in the town, consistent with the Dedoplistsqaro coordinate given in the brief.

Coordinate is the centroid of OSM relation 6135120 (tagged boundary=national_park, wikidata Q2097137); Wikipedia's infobox instead gives 41.200/46.383 and Wikidata 41.2/46.38333, both of which fall in the western half of the polygon.

The national park (IUCN II, WDPA 555549413, rel 6135120) and the strict reserve (IUCN Ia, ref:WDPA 1660, rel 6135198, Q12864387) are distinct legal entities; candidates 2 and 3 are correctly separate, not duplicates.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve (State Nature Reserve)
sites.description: Founded 1935 on the initiative of Niko Ketskhoveli and Vasil Guliashvili; IUCN category Ia, 10,143 ha of which 4,032 ha forest, the rest fields, semi-desert and ravines, at 300-600 m. The management plan states explicitly that the reserve contains NO zones, unlike the national park. Strictly off-limits to general visitors — the Pantishara route only overlooks it from the Nagomrebi side. Coordinate is the published Wikipedia/Wikidata point (41°09'17.5"N 46°32'49.6"E); OSM relation 6135198 centroid is 41.18336/46.47532.

sites.description: One of the three natural monuments of Vashlovani Protected Areas and one of Georgia's first (2003), 100.4 ha in two parts: a limestone rock canyon and an adjoining forest holding the 5th-century Khornabuji fortress. Habitat for 60-80 bird species including nesting black stork, griffon vulture and the endangered Egyptian vulture, plus the endemic Kakhetian bellflower (Campanula kakhetica) growing on bare limestone. Two pedestrian routes: 1 km / 1 h through the canyon and 0.5 km / 30 min to the fortress; 4 km north of Dedoplistsqaro (2 km paved + 2 km gravel, 15 min). Coordinate converted from the official UTM zone 38N value X 591747 / Y 4593825; agrees with the OSM gorge polygon (41.49286/46.09776) and Wikipedia (41.48774/46.09435). Lies west of the task bbox because the monument is outside the NP polygon, next to the town. 4 ha were transferred to the Khornabuji and Hereti Eparchy for 20 years by Presidential decree №747 of 30 Dec 2007.

Georgian-language sources confirm the candidate's disputed numbers over English Wikipedia's: the monument was established in 2003 with an area of 100.4 ha, whereas English Wikipedia's infobox gives 174 ha and 1935 (1935 is the strict reserve's date, wrongly inherited). Campanula kakhetica as Georgia's only local endemic, the black stork and griffon vulture, and the 1 km / 0.5 km route lengths are all independently corroborated. in_park_area=false: measured against the NP polygon the monument is 28.2 km from the nearest boundary — part of the Vashlovani Protected Areas administrative complex, but nowhere near the park or Chachuna. Its position west of the task's lon screen is genuine, not an error.

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument (Kaklis Kure / Walnut Bay)
sites.description: 204.4 ha of liana-hung riparian forest at 165 m in a peninsula-shaped bight of the Alazani riverbed, the only stretch of the river where the floodplain forest survives intact and the only place in Georgia with extensive natural stands of common walnut, oak, ash and elm — hence the name Walnut Bay. The entry neck is only 30-40 m wide and the forest is so dense that 1 km of the pedestrian route takes an hour. 56-60 km from Dedoplistsqaro (~1.5 h); entrance fee 5 GEL; picnic area at the monument. Coordinate is the official value N41 21.548 E46 39.235 from nationalparks.ge, corroborated by the OSM locality node კაკლის ყურე at 41.36568/46.65535. NOTE: English Wikipedia's infobox coordinate 41.69917/46.06444 is wrong and contradicts its own text.

sites.description: Inorganic natural monument of 9.7 ha total (the crater field itself ~1 ha) at 620 m on the plain south of the Dali water reservoir, parallel to the Takhti-Tepha range: a whitish flat-topped knoll of sandstone and clay whose craters and vents continuously erupt mud, oil and gas, the largest crater 3.5-4 m across, mud heights 20 cm to 1.5 m. Pedestrian path 0.5 km / 30 min; entrance 5 GEL. 37 km from Dedoplistsqaro — gravel road to the Dali reservoir on the Iori, then 15 km further. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: lon 45.844 is ~35 km west of the park bbox and outside the brief's sanity range. The coordinate is nonetheless well attested — I converted the official UTM 38N value X 570695 / Y 4566331 from nationalparks.ge to 41.24530/45.84372, which matches Wikipedia's independently published 41.245683/45.843617 to within metres — and the westward position is consistent with the official 37 km driving distance and with the monument being a detached unit of the protected-areas complex.

Independent corroboration beyond the cited sources: the official Vashlovani trekking map PDF (nationalparks.ge, extracted directly from the PDF streams) states that in 2003 Vashlovani NP and Georgia's first Natural Monuments - 'Alazani Floodplain Forest (Kaklis Kure), Takhti-Tepa and Eagle Gorge' - were established; AllTrails, ioverlander, Reinis Fischer, Georgian Travel Guide and Tushetiland all list it as a visitable mud-volcano field. COORDINATE: I re-did the UTM arithmetic myself rather than trusting the claim. Official UTM 38N X 570695 / Y 4566331 (from nationalparks.ge) inverse-projects to 41.245296 / 45.843723; Wikipedia's independently published 41 deg 14.741' N, 45 deg 50.617' E = 41.245683 / 45.843617. The two agree to ~50 m, and the candidate's 41.24530 / 45.84372 is the UTM value to 5 dp. So the coordinate is right; I give the Wikipedia decimal as corrected_lat/lon only as the marginally better published value, not as a correction of substance. Attributes verified: 9.7 ha total (crater field ~1 ha), 620 m elevation, 'on plane, south of Dali water reservoir' (Wikipedia + nationalparks.ge); 37 km from Dedoplistsqaro, gravel road to the Dali reservoir then dirt, 0.5 km / 30 min pedestrian path (nationalparks.ge); 5 GEL entrance ('Entrance fee at Takhti-Tefa Nature Monument - 5 GEL', apa.gov.ge tariff page). NOT verified: the 3.5-4 m largest crater and 20 cm-1.5 m mud heights - nationalparks.ge gives no crater dimensions. IN-AREA CAVEAT (measured, not asserted): I fetched the OSM Chachuna boundary relation 6134985 geometry, assembled its 14 rings and ran point-in-polygon - Takhti-Tepa is NOT inside Chachuna; nearest boundary vertex is 3.98 km away. It is therefore neither in the NP nor in Chachuna, but it is an official constituent unit of Vashlovani Protected Areas and Budget Bucket List reports that visiting the mud volcanoes requires a Chachuna Managed Reserve permit, so I score in_park_area=true with that 4 km caveat stated explicitly. DUPLICATE WATCH: Takhti-Tepa is routinely paired with the Kilakupra mud volcanoes (a separate nearby field, e.g. the AllTrails 'Kilakupra and Takhti-Tepha' route) - if Kilakupra appears as another candidate it is a different site, not a duplicate. No confusion with Vashlovani village in Abkhazia.

sites.description: 5,200 ha IUCN Category IV reserve (est. 1996) protecting a strip of Iori river tugay floodplain forest (aspen Populus tremula, long-stalk oak, white willow) plus arid light forest of wild pistachio and juniper, semi-desert and steppe on the surrounding hills and escarpment, and the Dalis-Mta reservoir. 82 bird species including imperial eagle, griffon vulture, black francolin; lynx, jungle cat, red fox, badger, wild boar, probable striped hyena; Greek tortoise and Levantine viper (Macrovipera lebetina). NACRES rated it a secondary gazelle reintroduction site with full habitat connectivity to Vashlovani. CONFIDENCE LOW: coordinate lies west of the supplied bbox (the reserve itself is genuinely SW of the NP). Wikipedia gives 41.29972/45.8925; the OSM boundary centroid is 41.18375/46.09831 — both fall within this long, narrow riverine reserve.
sites.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED on every checkable point. Existence is beyond doubt: Wikipedia, Georgia.travel (state tourism administration), Birdingplaces, Georgian Holidays and Budget Bucket List all describe a 5,200 ha managed reserve established 1996 in Dedoplistsqaro municipality protecting the Iori floodplain forests and the Dalis-Mta (Dali) reservoir. COORDINATE - tested, not assumed: I downloaded the OSM boundary relation 6134985 ('chachunas agkvetili' / Chachuna Managed Reserve, wikidata Q12871259, source 'apa.gov.ge map'), assembled its 14 closed rings (2,195 vertices) and ran a ray-casting point-in-polygon test. The supplied 41.29972 / 45.8925 IS INSIDE the reserve polygon (0.56 km from the nearest boundary vertex). Independent second opinion: Birdingplaces publishes 41.308931 / 45.914306 for the same reserve, 2.2 km away and effectively on the boundary. So the coordinate is good and needs no correction. Reserve OSM bbox is lat 41.17188-41.35885, lon 45.81184-46.23701 - a long reserve straddling the Iori, which is why it legitimately sits west of the brief's 46.2-46.8 window; the brief itself names Chachuna as in scope, so in_park_area=true. ONE CORRECTION TO THE CANDIDATE'S OWN WORKING: the candidate reports 'the OSM boundary centroid is 41.18375/46.09831'. Overpass 'out center' for relation 6134985 actually returns 41.265367 / 46.024427, and that point is NOT inside the polygon (6.31 km outside) because it is a bbox centre of a concave multi-ring shape. The candidate's 41.18375/46.09831 does test inside, but it is not what Overpass returns, so that specific provenance claim is unreliable even though the conclusion (both points fall within the reserve) survives for its own figure. Use the Wikipedia point. Ecology claims (imperial eagle, black francolin, lesser kestrel, tugay forest, Dali reservoir) are corroborated by Birdingplaces and Georgian Holidays; the NACRES gazelle-reintroduction ranking and the 82-species count I could not independently re-verify. No duplicate/transliteration problem: 'Chachuna' / 'chachunas agkvetili' / 'Zakaznik Chachuni' are one place.

sites.description: One of the eight permanent 24-hour ranger protection stations listed in the 2013 management plan, and the operational hub deepest inside the park. Coordinate is OSM way 474150182, tagged building=office, name "rangerpost", standing ~40 m from the Central Bungalows compound — the two form one enclosure. Rangers here run scheduled weekly patrol routes assigned per sector; in 2013 the protection division comprised a head, 2 senior rangers and 23 rangers.

The nearest named OSM features are the Mlashetskali river and the 'Kasristskali-Mijniskure' road, so the locality is more plausibly Kasristskali/Karistskali. DUPLICATE WARNING: this candidate and candidate 4 are the same site 41 m apart - a GIS layer must merge them or label one clearly as a sub-feature of the other, or the map will show two pins on one compound.

sites.name_en: Mijniskure visitor facility and bungalow camp

sites.description: Zone where local people exercise limited use of renewable natural resources, principally winter sheep grazing — a tradition still practised, with shepherds' huts strung along route 8 from October to May and lambing from February to April. Every distinctive element of the candidate description (45 m, Kochebi Lake, Shiraki, Taribana, Kotsakhura) is verified, including the 45 m vs 60 m source conflict — the APA sightseeing page independently says 'built on limestone rock at 60-meter height, 3 km south of Dedoplistskaro, V-VI century'. So the candidate's '5th-7th century' and the 45/60 m discrepancy are both faithfully reported, not invented.

IN_PARK_AREA = FALSE. At 41.442/46.109 it is ~2.4 km south of Dedoplistsqaro and ~20 km outside the park's west edge (46.27756) — well outside the task's lon 46.2–46.8 window. An Overpass is_in at this point returned only Georgia / Kakheti / Dedoplistsqaro Municipality plus two untagged ways: no protected-area polygon. It is also not inside Artsivi Gorge NM, which lies north of the town while this is south; the trekking map files it under 'NEARBY TOURIST ATTRACTIONS'.

One factual slip in the candidate: it calls this the 'second waypoint of route 1'. In the official route-1 (Artsivis Kheoba) narrative the order is gorge entrance → limestone cliffs with Campanula kakhetica → vulture viewpoints → Khornabuji fortress → St Elias Mountain, so it is the last, not the second, waypoint. Also note the 'Gombori Range' framing is consistent, not a red flag: Wikipedia places nearby Khornabuji on the Tsiv-Gombori Range, so the Commons category is not evidence of a mix-up with a different Mount Elia.

sites.description: The park's signature canyon, 50-55 km from the visitor centre and the start of routes 2, 7 and 8. Vertical fortress-like cliffs on both sides; the road in runs along the boundary between two landscapes, with the delicate xerophytic Nagomrebi ridge on the right and the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve 50-70 m below on the left. The management plan lists it among the arid-woodland and clay-badland landscape units and notes the gorge bed is dry most of the year. Coordinate is OSM node 11792574788 (tourism=attraction); a Pantishara Valley board sits at 41.22787/46.35112 and a Pantishara plain board at 41.19274/46.35700.
sites.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL AND IN THE PARK, with genuinely independent scientific corroboration. Greń C, Dobosz R, Bunalski M, Lasoń A, Lubecki K, Wąsala R, Japoshvili G (2023), 'A new species and family of beetle for Georgia (Sakartvelo): Arrhaphipterus schelkownikoffi', Caucasiana 2: 165–169, doi:10.3897/caucasiana.2.e110290 — I downloaded the article XML and its material-examined section reads: 'Kakheti, Vashlovani National Park, Pantishara canyon; 41°14'15"N, 46°21'55"E; 392 m a.s.l.; 6 August 2021; UV trap', and Figure 5B is captioned 'Vashlovani National Park, Pantishara canyon. Collecting site ... with UV trap shown.' That coordinate converts to 41.2375/46.36528, i.e. ~0.7 km from the supplied 41.23153/46.36246 — same canyon, different point along a linear feature. This is corroboration from a peer-reviewed source with no relationship to the cited park websites.

I also verified OSM myself: node 11792574788 exists at 41.2315298/46.3624627, tourism=attraction, პანტიშარას კანიონი / 'Pantishira Canyon'. And I extracted the official trekking-map PDF text directly, which confirms the route claims precisely: route 2 'Pantishara – Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge)', 'distance from the visitor center to Pantishara Gorge – 55 km'; route 7 'Bugha Moedani – Shavi Mta' and route 8 'Land of the hidden water' both give 'visitor center > Pantishara Gorge ... – 50 km'. So 'the start of routes 2, 7 and 8' and '50-55 km from the visitor centre' are exactly right. The map also describes 'Pantishara Alesilebi (razor-sharp badlands cliffs) that at first sight look like man-made castles' — supporting the 'fortress-like cliffs' wording. The matsne management plan (order №53, 2013) mentions პანტიშარა in its landscape/hydrology descriptions.

Location check: 41.2315/46.3625 is inside the authoritative park bbox and inside the OSM Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve relation's bounds (rel 6135198, 41.0977–41.2691 N, 46.3089–46.6418 E), consistent with the candidate's own statement that the access road runs along the NP/Strict Reserve boundary.

Caveats: (a) 'Pantishara' has no Wikidata item and no Wikimedia Commons media — coverage is thin outside APA/OSM and entomological literature; (b) the 'Nagomrebi ridge' and '50–70 m below on the left' details could not be corroborated in the management plan excerpt I retrieved — treat as unverified; (c) a single node is a weak representation of a multi-kilometre canyon, so the exact point is arbitrary rather than wrong; (d) NOT a duplicate of candidates 4 or 5 — see those verdicts.

sites.name_en: Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge) and its picnic site
sites.description: Side gorge off Pantishara carrying the park's palaeontological walking trail, and one of the seven picnic sites designated in the management plan. Fossilised woody plants and seashells are exposed between rock layers, proving the area was once under water, and southern-elephant bones were excavated here. Coordinate is OSM node 11792582004, name "დათვისხევი" / name:en "Bear Canyon"; a second board "დათვის ხევი" sits at 41.23769/46.36554.
sites.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL AND IN THE PARK, including the specific 'seven picnic sites' claim, which I verified in the primary legal text rather than taking on trust. The Vashlovani Protected Areas Management Plan (matsne.gov.ge doc 1971216, ministerial order №53 of 2 Aug 2013), Article 28 on eco-tourism, lists: '7 საპიკნიკე ადგილი (დათვის ხევი, ვაშლოვანი, ცენტრალური ბუნგალოები, მიჯნისყურე, ტახისწყალი, შავი მთა, კაკლის ყურე)' — seven picnic sites, the first being დათვის ხევი (Datvis Khevi / Bear Gorge). Exactly as claimed.

I extracted the official trekking-map PDF text directly; it confirms the palaeontological content verbatim: 'From the gorge visitors can follow Datviskhevi hiking trail ... unveiling extraordinary attractions – fossilized woody plants and seashells that can be seen between the layers of rocks. These remains prove that surrounding territories were under water a long time ago. On the Datviskhevi trail the fossils of bones of a Southern elephant have been found, the largest of which, 87 cm in length ... (nowadays bones excavated here are kept in the Protected Areas administration building).' nationalparks.ge route 6 independently repeats the 87 cm shoulder bone.

Coordinate: I re-queried OSM and node 11792582004 exists at exactly 41.2382717/46.3657870, tourism=attraction, name დათვისხევი / name:en 'Bear Canyon'. Independent cross-check: the Greń et al. 2023 collecting coordinate for 'Pantishara canyon' (41.2375/46.36528) sits only ~100 m from this node, which is exactly what you would expect for a side gorge opening off Pantishara. Inside the park bbox and inside the OSM Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve bounds.

TRANSLITERATION / DUPLICATE NOTE: დათვისხევი, დათვის ხევი, Datviskhevi, Datvis Khevi, 'Bear Gorge' and OSM's 'Bear Canyon' are all one and the same feature. The candidate's own note that a second board 'დათვის ხევი' sits at 41.23769/46.36554 (~60 m away) is a duplicate OSM board for the same place, not a second site — do not ingest both as separate records. It is a distinct feature from candidate 3 (Pantishara is the main canyon; Datviskhevi is the named side gorge with the palaeontological trail and the designated picnic site), so 3 and 4 are not duplicates of each other despite being ~800 m apart.

sites.description: Named cliff face in the Pantishara gorge where swallows have colonised the vertical rock in such numbers that the park calls it a city; a headline attraction of route 2. Coordinate is the OSM interpretive node 4424086000, name "მერცხლების ქალაქი" / name:en "city of swallows".
sites.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL AND IN THE PARK, with one framing caveat. I extracted the official Vashlovani trekking-map PDF text myself: route 2 'Pantishara – Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge)' lists as its first main attraction 'city of swallows', and the narrative says 'Visitors admire very unusual attractions they can find here – in the cliffs swallows have built their city and dwell here in abundance.' I separately fetched nationalparks.ge route 6, which independently states the gorge is 'called the City of Swallows' and that on the vertical cliffs 'swallows have built their nests'. I re-queried OSM and node 4424086000 exists at exactly 41.2366228/46.3669281, tourism=information, with names in four languages: მერცხლების ქალაქი / 'city of swallows' / 'Stadt der Schwalben' / 'город ласточек'. Coordinate verified as supplied; it is inside the park bbox and inside the OSM Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve bounds (41.0977–41.2691 N, 46.3089–46.6418 E).

CAVEAT ON THE DESCRIPTION: the candidate calls it a 'named cliff face', but neither official source delimits a single discrete cliff. The park's own wording attaches the name to the swallow-colonised badlands cliffs of the Pantishara gorge generally, and nationalparks.ge applies it to the gorge. The OSM feature is tourism=information — an interpretive board, which the candidate does correctly acknowledge — so the point marks the board/viewpoint, not a surveyed rock face. Treat the geometry as a signpost location with roughly gorge-scale uncertainty, not a precise landform.

Corroboration outside the park's own publications is thin: there is no Wikidata item and no Wikimedia Commons media for it, and Bing/DuckDuckGo were unusable from this environment (CAPTCHA / irrelevant results), so I could not find a Georgian-language third-party write-up. Two independent official APA channels plus OSM are enough to clear exists=true, but this is the weakest-sourced of the five.

DUPLICATE NOTE: at 207 m from the Datviskhevi node and ~600 m from the Pantishara canyon node, candidates 3, 4 and 5 form one tight cluster at the same gorge complex. They are nonetheless three separate named attractions in the park's own route description (main canyon / palaeontological side gorge / swallow cliffs), so they should be kept as three records — but a map that renders them as three independent pins will overstate how far apart they are.

sites.description: Viewpoint over the Alesilebi — razor-sharp eroded badland cliffs that look like man-made castles but are erosional pillars and columns; the park's most-photographed geology and listed as a highlight of routes 2, 6 and 7. Coordinate is OSM viewpoint node 11891968791 (ალესილების ხედი). A "Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi" road runs to it (way centre 41.24299/46.40687).
sites.verify_reasoning: Confirmed independently of the cited sources. OSM node 11891968791 re-fetched directly from api.openstreetmap.org: lat 41.2232178, lon 46.3526434, tags name=ალესილების ხედი ('view of Alesilebi'), tourism=viewpoint. An OSM tourism=information board (node 10836252052) sits ~40 m away at 41.2235/46.3532, so this is a developed, signposted stop rather than an isolated hand-placed node. Surrounding OSM context fits the description: 'პანტიშარას ხეობა / Pantissara Valley' info node 600 m north (41.2279/46.3511), 'პანტიშარას კანიონი / Pantishira Canyon' attraction 1.2 km NE (41.2315/46.3625), and way 48844795 'Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi' tagged both highway=unclassified and waterway=river — i.e. the access track runs in a dry riverbed, matching independent trip reports of driving the Pantishara riverbed. Independent (non-cited) corroboration that Alesilebi is a real named badlands feature: dtda.ge (Dedoplistsqaro Tourism Development Agency) Pantishara-Datviskhevi trail page describes the trail passing through 'Alesilebi', 'a vast panoramic area of eroded badlands'; wander-lush.org describes 'Alesilebi Seabeds' with marine sediment, corals and shells in the canyon walls; goingthewholehogg.com lists 'Alesilebi rock formations' and 'Pantishara Viewpoint' among park highlights. Coordinate is inside lat 41.0-41.5 / lon 46.2-46.8 and inside the OSM Vashlovani National Park polygon (relation 6135120) by point-in-polygon test. SRTM elevation at the point is 324 m, within the park's 78-858 m range. Two caveats, neither fatal: (a) the candidate name fuses two distinct named features — 'Pantishara' (the valley/canyon) and 'Alesilebi' (the badlands) — which are separate entries in both OSM and the guides, so joining on this name risks colliding with a separate 'Pantishara Viewpoint' candidate; (b) the 'road runs to it, way centre 41.24299/46.40687' note is misleading — that is the centroid of a long road way, ~7 km from the viewpoint, not a location for this site.

sites.description: Marked locality on the Datviskhevi trail where the fossil bones of a southern elephant (Archidiskodon meridionalis) were excavated, the largest a shoulder bone about 87 cm long; the excavated material is now held in the protected areas administration building in Dedoplistsqaro. The park also advertises million-year-old plant and animal fossils and mammoth remains on its territory. Coordinate is OSM node 11792396535 (tourism=attraction).
sites.verify_reasoning: Confirmed. OSM node 11792396535 re-fetched directly: lat 41.2455262, lon 46.3686595, tourism=attraction, name:en 'Fossil elephant bone finding place', name:ka ნამარხი სპილოს ძვლების პოვნის ადგილი. Independent corroboration from sources NOT cited by the researcher: dtda.ge (Dedoplistsqaro Tourism Development Agency) Pantishara-Datviskhevi page — 'The highlight of the route is the fossilized bones of the southern elephant, the largest of which reaches 87cm'; georgiantravelguide.com Pantishara-Datvis Khevi page; trekgeorgia.com, which states 'a fossilized scapula of the southern elephant is protruding from the clay hill'. The 87 cm figure and the southern-elephant identification therefore reproduce across at least three sources independent of the park website. OSM context strongly supports the location: the Datviskhevi trailhead cluster sits ~1 km SSW at 41.2373/46.3655 with an interpretive board named 'The Fossilized World of Vashlovani' (node 10836242519), a trail map board 'Pantishara - Datvis Khevi (Bear Gorge) Trail' (node 10836250941), a camp site, a picnic site, and attraction nodes 'დათვის ხევი / bear ravine' and 'დათვისხევი / Bear Canyon'; an 'end of car way' node at 41.2428/46.3695 lies 300 m from the fossil node, i.e. the fossil point is up the walking section of the gorge exactly as described. Coordinate is inside the stated lat/lon window and inside the park bounding box (46.27756-46.73632 / 41.09400-41.35038), in the Pantishara gorge corridor between the National Park polygon and the Strict Nature Reserve polygon. Elevation 446 m (SRTM), plausible. One unsupported detail: the claim that the excavated material 'is now held in the protected areas administration building in Dedoplistsqaro' is not corroborated anywhere I could find, and trekgeorgia explicitly describes the scapula as still in situ in the clay. Treat that sentence as embellishment; the site itself is real. The 'mammoth remains' phrasing is also loose — the animal is Archidiskodon (Mammuthus) meridionalis, a southern elephant, not a woolly mammoth.

sites.name_en: Ancient pistachio grove (oldest pistachio tree in Europe)
sites.description: Grove of wild pistachio (Pistacia, Georgian საკმლის ხე) reached by a short trail from the Vashlovani ranger station: most trees are over 500 years old and the oldest is over 900, advertised as the oldest pistachio in Europe. The species is Red-Listed in Georgia and abundant here; the park's name is popularly explained by the resemblance of these open pistachio stands to apple orchards. Coordinate is the OSM natural=tree node 10836240203 ("Old Pistachio"), with a "Flora" interpretive board at the same point.
sites.verify_reasoning: The place is real and the coordinate is right, but the headline superlative in the name is NOT independently supported. OSM node 10836240203 re-fetched directly: lat 41.2080283, lon 46.4360255, natural=tree, name 'Old Pistachio'. A tourism=information board tagged information=board, name='Flora' (node 10836192448) is at 41.2079995/46.4360255 — the same point to 4 decimal places — so the tree is a signposted interpretive stop, which is good evidence it is a curated park feature and not a random mapper's tree. The Vashlovani ranger-station cluster is ~800 m north (camp_site node 1182749665 at 41.2154/46.4334, 'Vaschlovani Horse Ranche' info node, picnic site, guidepost, board), matching 'reached by a short trail from the Vashlovani ranger station'. Point-in-polygon against OSM relation 6135198 puts it inside the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve (IUCN Ia, WDPA 1660) rather than inside the National Park polygon proper — still squarely within the Vashlovani Protected Areas complex and inside the stated park bbox, so in_park_area holds. Elevation 468 m. Independent corroboration of an ancient-pistachio walking trail: wander-lush.org describes an 'Eldest Tree Trail' with 'perennial pistachio trees'. However, wander-lush gives the age as 'some of which are 400 years old', whereas the candidate asserts 'most trees over 500 years old and the oldest over 900'. I could find that 500/900 wording ONLY in the single cited Henry Lebt route PDF (a scan of park signage), with no second source, and I found NO source at all — Georgian or otherwise — making the 'oldest pistachio in Europe' claim. That superlative should be dropped or attributed to park signage. Also note the candidate calls this a 'grove' but the coordinate is a single-tree node; the grove is the surrounding stand, and pistachio-juniper stands (საკმლისხიან-ღვიიანი კორომები) are confirmed for the park by Georgian Wikipedia. The gloss that the park's name ('place of apples') comes from pistachio stands resembling apple orchards is a folk etymology I could not corroborate.

sites.name_en: Usakhelo Mta (Nameless Mountain) and Usakhelo viewpoint
sites.description: Peak of 428 m whose massif is one of the three named viewpoints in the management plan and the panorama over the badlands that routes 5 and 6 cross before descending to Mijniskure. The whole Usakhelo massif, with the lower Natlistskali and the Mijniskure gorge, forms the national park's strict nature protection zone. Coordinate is the OSM peak node 8061747863 (უსახელო-მთა, ele=428).
sites.verify_reasoning: Confirmed, with one naming caveat. OSM node 8061747863 re-fetched directly: lat 41.1191402, lon 46.6095466, natural=peak, ele=428, name უსახელო-მთა / name:ru 'Усахело - Мта'. I tested the summit claim rather than trusting the tag: a 7x7 SRTM30m grid sampled at +/-0.005/0.010/0.020 degrees around the node returns 420 m at the node itself and a next-highest neighbour of 350 m, so the node is an unambiguous local maximum and the 428 m tag is consistent with SRTM (420 m) after smoothing. Independent corroboration of the viewpoint (sources not cited by the researcher): ountravela.com — 'A dirt track leads to the spectacular Usakhelo viewpoint. An observation platform has been built above an outcrop, offering panoramic views of badlands'; goingthewholehogg.com lists 'Usakhelo Viewpoint' among park highlights; wander-lush.org calls it the author's favourite vista with 'a gangway viewing platform'; AllTrails lists a 'Usakhelo Viewpoint' trail. The official nationalparks.ge Mijniskure-Shavi Mta route independently states 'Through Usakhelo Viewing Point, the trail goes down to Mijniskure' and lists 'View of Usakhelo' as a highlight, matching the description exactly; Mijniskure is confirmed in OSM at 41.1111/46.6467 (მიჯნის ყურე). Caveat: the candidate merges two features under one coordinate. The supplied coordinate is the PEAK. The developed viewing platform in OSM near it is a separate node, 4006544463 'დევების გადასახედი' (name:en 'viewpoint canyons') at 41.1275/46.6072, ~950 m north, co-located with a 'Canyons' interpretive board (node 10836251299 at 41.1272/46.6071). If the intent is the tourist platform, use 41.1275/46.6072; as published for the peak, the coordinate is correct, so I leave it unchanged.

sites.description: Broad semi-desert plain in the south of the protected areas, giving its name to route 7 and hosting the goitered gazelle enclosure and its protection station. The management plan places it in the plains semi-desert landscape together with the middle and lower Lekistskali flats, and records that isolated gazelles survived on Bugha Moedani and the Qumuro flats until the end of the 20th century. Coordinate is OSM viewpoint node 4867606321; the plateau node 9677524553 is at 41.13247/46.53878.
sites.verify_reasoning: Confirmed. Independent corroboration for the protection-station and gazelle claims, from sources not cited by the researcher: a Council of Europe on-the-spot expert appraisal of the Vashlovani Protected Areas lists 'Bugha moedani' as one of six Protection Stations in the reserve alongside Mijniskure and the Central bungalows — that is an authoritative, non-OSM, non-park-marketing source for both the name and the station; caucastours.com describes driving 'through Bughamoedani to Samukhi plains' where 'Raptors and the goitered gazelle can be sighted'. The official nationalparks.ge route list independently carries a route named 'Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta'. The enclosure claim is supported by imagery-independent OSM evidence I pulled myself: way 1053053005 is a barrier=fence with height=2 forming a closed perimeter spanning 41.1242-41.1272 N / 46.5356-46.5387 E (roughly 330 x 250 m, 34 nodes) whose southeast corner is essentially on the viewpoint node, with an OSM camp_site tagged name:en 'Ranger Station' 140 m away at 41.1256/46.5386 — a 2 m stock fence enclosing a paddock beside a ranger station is exactly what a gazelle acclimatisation enclosure looks like. The nearby way 1067617513 named კუმრა / 'kumra' corroborates the 'Qumuro/Kumuro flats' toponym in the description (same place, different transliteration — worth normalising if a separate Kumuro candidate exists elsewhere in the set). Signed viewpoint over the canyon country on the Mijniskure road, with an accompanying "Canyons" interpretive board at 41.12720/46.60712. Coordinate is OSM viewpoint node 4006544463, name "დევების გადასახედი" / name:en "viewpoint canyons". Mapped on OSM but not individually named in the official documents, which list only three viewpoints (Vashlovani, Usakhelo, Shavi Mta).

Viewpoint in the park interior on the Vashlovani-Mijniskure axis, mapped as OSM viewpoint node 11553249495 (ექოს გადასახედი). Present on the mapping platform but not named in the official APA documents.

Broad valley in the west of the park reached from Pantishara on route 8 and the best place to see reintroduced goitered gazelle from a distance; approaching them is prohibited. sites.name_en: Natlistskali / Lekistskali gorge and its saline springs
sites.description: The gorge that holds the park's 9 central bungalows. The management plan treats Natlistskali and Lekistskali as the same watercourse, places steppe in its upper reach and the strict protection zone in its lower reach, and notes that the very low-yield saline springs emerging at the head of the gorge dry up on the spot. A section of the Silk Road ran through this gorge together with Qumuro and the Eldari lowland. Coordinate is the OSM board "ლეკის (მლაშე) წყალი" (salty water), node 4424146494; the Mlashetskali river ways run at 41.12590/46.60557 and 41.21056/46.54420.

Signed gorge on the Mijniskure-Takhistskali side of the park, named for its exposed shales. Coordinate is the OSM interpretive node 4424146495 (ფიქალების ხევი). Mapped and signed on the ground but not named in the official documents.

sites.name_en: Alazani river border reach and border-river viewpoint
sites.description: The Alazani forms the state border with Azerbaijan along the park's southern and eastern edge; the protected areas stretch between the Alazani and the Iori. Its right bank holds the floodplain forests, jungle cat, otter and introduced raccoon tracks, and the park's licensed fly fishing. A trans-boundary rafting route on the Alazani is named in the management plan as a cooperation objective with Azerbaijan. Coordinate is the OSM viewpoint node 10081554153 "სასაზღვრო მდინარე ალაზანი" (Border Alazani River); the river way ალაზანი-Qanıx centres at 41.34126/46.51714.

sites.name_en: Iori (Yori / Qabırlı) river and Iori canal
sites.description: The western and southern limit of the protected-areas complex, which stretches between the Iori and the Alazani on the Iori upland. The upland plain north of the park, visible to the east from the church on Mount Elias and crossed by the Dedoplistskaro-Pantishara track. Reservoir north of the park on the Kasristskali-Vashlovani approach, mapped as a camp site (OSM node 6795686586, tourism=camp_site, "შირაქის ხელოვნური ტბა" / Shiraqi Lake). Not one of the four campsites designated in the management plan, so it is an informal or non-park site rather than official park infrastructure.

Salt lake of 0.38 km2, Wikidata Q24687078 with a Georgian Wikipedia article; OSM way/1499013398 and relation/20443025; GeoNames 866042 'Ozero Kochebi' classes it H.LKN salt lake at 41.44104, 46.14569, dem 777 m. Named on the Eagle Gorge route as visible east from the St Elias church. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window.

sites.name_en: Green Lake and Three Brothers, Eagle Gorge
sites.description: Small lake inside the Eagle Gorge Natural Monument (OSM way 1307001807, მწვანე ტბა), with a signed "სამი ძმა" (Three Brothers) feature 10 m away at 41.49862/46.09890 and a "სახოხბე" board at 41.49958/46.10056. Mapped and signed on the ground; not individually named in the APA documents. West of the task bbox, consistent with the monument's position north of Dedoplistsqaro.

Camp site mapped at the head of the Eagle Gorge (OSM node 12103987907, tourism=camp_site). Not among the four campsites designated in the management plan, which cover only the national park proper, so this is most likely a concession or informal site at the natural monument. A spring, Mazovkis Tsqali, is mapped nearby at 41.47777/46.09495.

Georgian Border Police post inside the park in the far south, on the Pantishara-Eldari road close to the Azerbaijan frontier. The park lies in a border zone and the official rules require every visitor to carry an identity card and to register at the visitor centre before entering; deviating from marked trails is prohibited. Coordinate is OSM way 998796932 (amenity=police, "საქართველოს სასაზღვრო პოლიცია" / border checkpoint).

sites.name_en: Border police checkpoint, road to Mijniskure (Lekistskali)
sites.description: Border checkpoint on the Mijniskure road just south of the central bungalows, controlling the descent to the Alazani frontier. Mapped as OSM way 998800894 (amenity=police, "border checkpoint"). Relevant to the park's border-zone access regime: visits require prior registration and an ID card.

sites.name_en: Border police checkpoint, Takhistskali - Shavi Mta road (east)
sites.description: Border Police post on the eastern side of the park on the Takhistskali-Shavi Mta axis, close to the Alazani and the Azerbaijan border. Coordinate is OSM way 1105206643. A fourth post sits on the western approach at 41.17242/46.30120 (way 1105224457).

Remains of an ancient city inside the protected areas, listed by name in the official APA sightseeing text as the "City of Khoranta" among remains of ancient cities and villages. The same passage names the ruined villages of Upadara and Kaladara, for which no coordinate was found. Coordinate is OSM node 8927317168 (historic=ruins). The management plan notes that most of the territory is archaeologically unstudied.

Ruined iron-smelting workshop mapped inside the national park west of the Vashlovani basin (OSM node 8927317169, historic=ruins), part of the cluster of archaeological ruins recorded on the plateau between Pantishara and Mijniskure. Mapped on OSM only; not individually named in the APA documents, which do record ancient settlement and fortification remains across the territory.

Ancient settlement remains mapped in the Mijniskure area (OSM node 8927317167, historic=ruins). The APA sightseeing page independently records watchtowers in the Pantishara and Mijnis Kure gorges among the fortification remains of the protected areas, and the management plan repeats this, so a site of this kind at Mijniskure is expected. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: lat 41.0618 falls just south of the brief's sanity box and ~5 km south-west of the Mijniskure compound itself, and only one source carries it, so the position is unconfirmed.

sites.name_en: Pantishara and Mijnis Kure gorge watchtowers
sites.name_ka: პანტიშარის და მიჯნის ყურის ხეობების საგუშაგოები
sites.description: Ancient fortification remains named in both the official APA sightseeing text and the management plan's cultural-heritage article, alongside the Khornabuji city-fortress, the Choeti fortress and the Black Mountain monastery. No source gives coordinates and neither appears by name on the mapping platforms, so lat/lon is omitted rather than guessed from the gorge positions.

Medieval ruined town mapped on the Iori-side western edge of the protected areas (OSM node 8927317170, historic=ruins), on the Taribana-Chachuna-Eldari road corridor. Mapped on OSM only; the APA text records ancient cities and villages in the area generally.

The principal unpaved approach from the town to the Pantishara gorge, the spine of routes 2, 7 and 8 and plausibly one of the management plan's "3 main vehicle roads with beautiful views" (the plan does not name them). Mapped in OSM as several named ways tagged highway=track and highway=unclassified between 41.245/46.386 and 41.375/46.322; coordinate given is the centre of way 256957962. Off-road vehicles are required on park routes and motorbikes, quad bikes and helicopters are prohibited.

Interior track linking the Vashlovani basin and ranger station to Mijniskure, mapped in OSM as a chain of named ways (48845846, 287061800, 936722065, 936723034, 936723674) running roughly 41.175/46.554 to 41.210/46.455; coordinate is the centre of way 48845846. Parallel named corridors are Kasristskali-Mijniskure (centre 41.22406/46.52381) and Road to Mijniskure / მიჯნისყურის გზა (centre 41.13322/46.58244), the latter including several fords where the road runs in the stream bed.

Long southern traverse across the park between the Pantishara area and the Eldari lowland, mapped in OSM as a chain of some twenty named ways between about 41.105/46.478 and 41.210/46.359; coordinate is the centre of way 281481958. It follows the corridor of the semi-desert and clay-badland landscapes and passes close to the southern border police post.

Eastern track and footpath from the Takhistskali floodplain up to Shavi Mta, the ground route behind routes 5 and 7; mapped in OSM as named ways 496517609, 1349195377, 1349195379 and 1349195383 between about 41.163/46.652 and 41.203/46.613. Coordinate is the centre of way 496517609. Nominatim returns only these way segments for "Shavi Mta", which is how the Shavi Mta destination was located.

Northern approach from Kasristskali village into the Vashlovani basin, mapped in OSM as named ways 632756994, 632756995, 1337720734, 48845978, 632756996, 1337720733 and 1337720736 between about 41.232/46.432 and 41.280/46.453; coordinate is the centre of way 632756994. Kasristskali (41.28825/46.46372) is the nearest village with a town hall, school and ambulance station, on the northern rim of the park.

Western corridor linking the Taribana valley, the Chachuna Managed Reserve and the Eldari lowland along the Iori, mapped as OSM way 496517613. It is the natural access line towards the Dali reservoir and Takhti-Tepa on route 3, though no source states that correspondence.

Reservoir on the Iori, 35 km south-west of the visitor centre, the mid-point of route 3 and the landmark by which the official APA page fixes Takhti-Tepa ("to the south of Dali water reservoir"); the road to it is gravel and 15 km of rough road continue beyond. Wikipedia states that the Chachuna Managed Reserve encompasses the Dalis-Mta reservoir. A "Dali mountain hunting farm" is also offered as accommodation 45 km from the Eagle Gorge, and a Hotel Dalis Mta is listed on the park's accommodation page. Neither Overpass nor Nominatim returned a named feature, so no coordinate is given.

Gorge running from the central entrance of the national park to the Shavi Mta forest, the connecting leg of day 2 on routes 5 and 7. Named consistently in the official trekking map and on both trip pages (rendered variously as Imedi Gorge, Imedas Valley and Imelda's Valley). No source gives a coordinate and it is absent from Overpass and Nominatim under any spelling tried, so lat/lon is omitted.

Gorge traversed on day 2 of route 8 between Mijniskure and a park ranger station. The management plan lists Chighoetkhevi / Chighoelthkhevi twice among the steppe-landscape sectors, together with the upper Natlistskali gorge, Nagomrebi, Zilicha and Shavi Mta, which places it in the north-eastern steppe belt of the park. No published coordinate; absent from Overpass and Nominatim.

Ridge of delicate contours covered in xerophytic vegetation forming the right-hand side of the road into the Pantishara gorge, opposite the Strict Nature Reserve 50-70 m below on the left. The management plan lists Nagomrebi among the steppe-landscape sectors and among the Bothriochloa steppe areas at 200-600 m. No published coordinate; absent from Overpass and Nominatim.

The park's central structural basin, the viewpoint over which is a highlight of routes 2, 7 and 8 — an open space looking across pistachio trees and juniper shrubs. The management plan repeatedly names it as the best-preserved locality for the park's arid-woodland and gypsum-clay habitats and as a core area of the clay-badland landscape, and the trekking map calls it the Pantishara-Vashlovani massif at 300-600 m. The one purpose-built viewpoint of the three in the plan is "in Vashlovani". No discrete published coordinate.

Guest house mapped on the northern rim of the protected areas (OSM node 11833332872, tourism=guest_house). Plausibly one of the leased livestock farms in the traditional use zone now taking guests; the management plan records 31 such farms under lease and 45 using the park seasonally. Mapped on OSM only, not listed in the APA accommodation pages.

Family guest house listed on the official park site among accommodation around the park: 5 rooms, maximum 10 people, at 97 Megobrobis St, Dedoplistsqaro; contact Neli Gobejishvili, +995 599 19 63 35. The trekking map notes visitors can choose among several guest houses in the town in addition to the visitor centre hotel and the in-park bungalows and shelters. No coordinate published.

Shelter mapped on the northern approach to the park (OSM node 13065581331, amenity=shelter, name "Wiata" — Polish for a lean-to, suggesting a visitor-contributed name). Not referenced in any official source; included only because it is mapped visitor infrastructure in the approach corridor.

Camp site mapped between the Kasristskali-Vashlovani and Kasristskali-Pantishara tracks (OSM node 13294854338, tourism=camp_site, name "Wind protected"). The descriptive English name suggests a traveller-contributed pitch rather than official infrastructure; it is not one of the four campsites designated in the management plan.

Municipal centre and the gateway town for the whole complex, 130 km and about 2 hours from Tbilisi on a paved road; minibuses leave from Ortachala bus station and the station near Isani metro. Population about 15,000 of the municipality's 30,000. Holds the protected areas administration and visitor centre, guest houses, hotels and the Iliauni research centre (41.45813/46.12347). Coordinate is OSM node 388180700 (place=town, wikidata Q1010979); the brief's own value is 41.46389/46.11111.

One of the villages on route 4 to Kaklis Kure, which the official trip page lists as Zemo Kedi, Arkhilos Kalo and Kvemo Kedi. Has an ambulance station (41.37165/46.51105). Coordinate is OSM node 429443350 (wikidata Q4218649); Arkhiloskalo is at 41.40167/46.44583 per Wikidata and Pirosmani village — the reference point for the Alazani Floodplain monument — at 41.37397/46.56942.

sites.name_en: Domed Church of the Ascension, Ozaani
sites.description: 10th-century domed church with unique contemporary frescoes, in broad-leaved forest 19 km north-east of Dedoplistsqaro near the village of Ozaani (the trekking map says "near the village of Ozaani", 30 minutes by car). Listed by APA among the region's principal sightseeing points alongside the Seraphim of Sarov church at Samreklo (41.45316/46.13800), Bodbe Convent, Khirsa Monastery and the Niko Pirosmani house-museum at Mirzaani. Coordinate is the OSM place_of_worship node 5193319627. Well outside the park, north-west.

The park's flagship conservation asset rather than a point feature: Georgia's first successful reintroduction project, running since 2013, with up to about 150 goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) now on the protected areas after the species was poached out in the 1960s. Managed from the voliere and its protection station on Bugha Moedani inside the restoration zone; route 8 crosses the Samukhi valley where animals may be seen at a distance, and approaching them is prohibited. Ten of the 62 mammal species here are on Georgia's Red List; the park is the only place in Georgia where the endangered Egyptian vulture can be seen, and holds 135 bird, 20 fish, 30 reptile and 4 amphibian species and up to 700 plant species.

Not a site but the designation record for the complex, which totals 35,292 ha at 100-900 m and comprises the Strict Nature Reserve, the National Park and three natural monuments (Eagle Gorge, Takhti-Tepa, Alazani Floodplain/Kaklis Kure). Awarded the Council of Europe European Diploma of Protected Areas in 2015 and a member site of the Emerald Network. The national park management plan was approved by Minister's Order №53 of 2 Aug 2013, superseding the 2006 plan, and was revised with GIZ support under the "Sustainable management of biodiversity: South Caucasus" programme; earlier plans came from the Georgian Protected Area Programme, with WB/GEF ranger training and CNF, WWF and Norwegian government investment. Entrance fees are 5 GEL each for the national park, Takhti-Tepa and Alaznis Chala-Kaklis Kure.

IUCN Ia strict reserve founded 1935 (the original protected core), 84.80 km2 per the park article / 176.12 km2 per the reserve article, 300-600 m elevation, forest 4,032 ha with the remainder fields, semi-desert and ravines. Occupies the interior of the park between Pantishara and the Alazani; entry is restricted. English Wikipedia coordinate 41.15486, 46.54711; OSM polygon centroid 41.2504, 46.3552.

Dry wadi-like gorge at 359 m asl cut into the Neogene sandstone–clay–conglomerate pile of the Pantishara massif, alternately narrowing and opening out with sandcastle-like walls; APA official trail 2 runs through it from Kasristskali. An overhanging wall in mid-canyon carries a swallow 'town' of several thousand nests. Coordinate is the APA GPX waypoint; OSM independently places it at 41.23153/46.36246.

Named gorge/valley interpretation point on the upper Pantishara, tagged separately from the canyon narrows. The road to the gorge runs along the Nagomrebi ridge and then drops into the narrows. OSM node 4424146893.

Lower Pantishara open valley floor, marked as a named information point on the Pantishara-Eldari track south of the canyon narrows, on the way toward Samukhi and the Eldari lowland. OSM node 4424086001.

Side gorge off Pantishara with a 2.5-3 km hiking trail; fossilised wood, marine shells and the bones of a Southern elephant (Archidiskodon meridionalis) were excavated here, the largest bone 87 cm long (now in the protected-areas administration building). OSM attraction node 11792582004; a second 'bear ravine' info node sits at 41.23769, 46.36554.

The 'Alesilebi' (literally 'the sharpened ones') are erosion-carved clay/sandstone pillars and columns along Pantishara that look like man-made castles; PeakVisor describes the clay cliffs as rising 59-70 m. This is the named OSM viewpoint over them (node 11891968791); the formation itself has no single published point.

Interpretive point (OSM node/4424086000, name:ru 'город ласточек') at the Pantishara/Datviskhevi cliffs where swallows nest colonially in the eroded badland walls. Listed as a main attraction of official route 2.

FLAGGED: lon 46.096 is outside the supplied park bbox (~30 km NW, at Khornabuji village near Dedoplistsqaro), but this is a real 100.4 ha Natural Monument of the Vashlovani Protected Areas declared in 2003 and the coordinate comes from APA's own GPX (748 m; OSM viewpoint agrees at 41.49038/46.09770). Geologically it is the complex's only carbonate terrain — a deep narrow canyon cut by a small ravine into white limestone and limestone conglomerate, with the karst caves that park descriptions mention, in sharp contrast to the clastic badlands of the national park. Endemic limestone bellflower and Georgia's only thuja-like conifer stand; the 5th-c. Khornabuji fortress sits on the adjacent ridge at 41.486501/46.134301.

IUCN-III natural monument of the Vashlovani Protected Areas: a whitish flat-topped knoll of sandstone and clay with constantly active mud craters venting mud, oil and gas; largest crater 3.5-4 m across, total area 9.7 ha, 620 m a.s.l., 0.5 km pedestrian trail. Sits on the plain south of the Dali (Dalis-Mta) reservoir on the Iori. NOTE: the coordinate is ~35 km WEST of the national-park bounding box - the monument is a detached unit of the protected-areas complex, not inside the park. Wikipedia (41.245683, 45.843617) and the official nationalparks.ge UTM38N X 570695 / Y 4566331 (= 41.2453, 45.8437) agree to ~50 m.

OSM tourism=viewpoint labelled 'მ.ტახტი თეფა,763' (the 763 is probably a spot elevation), returned by Nominatim. It lies 6.5 km south-east of the apa.gov.ge/Wikipedia monument point, so it is likely an overlook on the Takhti-Tepha ridge rather than the crater field itself. LOW CONFIDENCE: unreconciled against the two agreeing authoritative points, and far outside the sanity window on longitude.

FLAGGED as outside the supplied park bbox (lon 45.770, ~45 km W of the park, Sighnaghi municipality, Kajiri valley, 410–450 m asl) — but the coordinate is solid: OSM node 4117121044 and Wikidata Q130746546 (41.333889/45.769722, 450 m) agree, and this is the best-studied mud volcano of the Iori plateau. The Kila-Kupra fold carries three separate vents, Kila-Kupra West, Central and East; Glonti et al. (IGCP 610, 2016) used 2D seismic to show they sit on a fault-complicated dome within an asymmetric anticline, and foraminifera in the mud breccia (Porosononion subgranosum, Nonion bogdanowiczi) indicate a Middle Sarmatian source rock, older than the Upper Sarmatian source previously assumed. Georgian alternative name 'მეორე ახტალა' (Second Akhtala); unpaved access, impassable in rain. Commonly sold as a package with Takhti-Tepa, which is why it is often described as a Vashlovani site.

sites.name_en: Zilcha (summit of the Shavi Mta massif)
sites.description: Highest named peak inside Vashlovani National Park: 845 m (OSM) / 846 m (Wikidata Q12864765). Stands at the eastern edge of the park above the Alazani, immediately above the Shavi Mta ranger post. PeakVisor lists it as the park's highest peak (847 m, prominence 217 m).
Ridge crest carrying the Zilcha summit, Wikidata Q125305823, 846 m, mapped ~1.3 km north of the peak node. Forms the spine of the Shavi Mta broadleaf-forest block on the park's eastern boundary.

Wooded ridge/massif in the eastern park, adjacent to Zilcha, and the only place in Vashlovani NP holding Mediterranean feathergrass steppe (EUNIS E1.432) — confined, per UNDP's pasture monitoring, to the Shavi Mta area on the slopes towards the Dilicha plain. Terminus of two park trails (Mijniskure - Shavi Mta; Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta) and of the 'Takhis tskali - Shavi mta' track; 4th-5th century monastery ruins on it. A 1984 Apodemus ponticus record sits at this coordinate; a 2025 Xeno-canto point 'Vashlovani reserve (Shavi Mta)' (Lullula arborea) at 41.26230/46.62790 corroborates the eastern position. CAUTION: two other sources place 'Shavi mta/Black Mountain' well away from here — eBird 41.24954/46.43225 and a Missouri Botanical Garden Pistacia voucher at 41.34513/46.53636; I judge those loose georeferences.

sites.name_en: Shavi Mta convent ruins (trailhead to the cross)
sites.description: 4th-5th century church, of which only floor fragments and foundations survive; by legend Queen Ketevan the Martyr spent her last night in Georgia here before being taken to Persia. The hiking trail runs along the ridge with broadleaf forest to the left and views of the Alazani valley and Mingachevir reservoir to the right. The coordinate is the OSM-mapped trailhead node ('footpath towards the cross', node 4424146592), not the ruins themselves.

428 m summit above Mijniskure in the far south-east of the park, mapped with an explicit elevation tag; a standard vantage over the eroded clay ridges and the Alazani floodplain, and the 'Usakhelo Viewpoint' of park itineraries. Mijniskure locality itself is at 41.11210/46.64827, with a ranger station at 41.111668/46.646137 (99 m).

Official viewpoint with a gangway platform on the track between the central park entrance and Mijniskure, overlooking the extensive badlands and canyon country; the brochure calls it the Usakhelo viewpoint. OSM node 4006544463, with a paired 'Canyons' interpretation node at 41.1272, 46.60712. Independently recorded at 41.1272, 46.6070 by a detailed field itinerary.

Named plateau ('Bull's Square') in the southern park, giving its name to the official two-day Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta route; a 'Semi-Desert' interpretation node sits nearby at 41.13231, 46.53041. OSM plateau node 9677524553 at 41.13247, 46.53878 and viewpoint node 4867606321 at 41.12431, 46.53801.
Named viewpoint in the interior of the park between Pantishara and the Mijniskure road. OSM node 11553249495.
Viewpoint over the Shiraki plain on the Dedoplistsqaro-Pantishara road, at the northern approach to the park. OSM node 8691353213.
Viewpoint over the Alazani where the river forms the Georgia-Azerbaijan border, just above Mijniskure at the southern tip of the park. OSM node 10081554153.

578 m mountain of the Iori Plateau in Kakheti, Wikidata Q12870536 (no English label). Sits on the north-western flank of the park between the Shiraki plain and the Iori. This is the best match found for the 'Kumuro' name; no source uses the spelling 'Kumuro' itself.

687 m named peak on the Iori-plateau rim west of the park (OSM node, elevation tagged 687 m). The separate Nazarlebi Early Iron Age Sanctuary and Settlement archaeological site lies ~6 km east at 41.33998, 46.24069. Longitude 46.17 is just west of the stated park bounding box.

Named hill inside the park, Wikidata Q24686779; PeakVisor lists 'Gora Komroy' at 370 m with 21 m prominence for Vashlovani National Park. Wikidata's coordinate is low-precision (whole-arcminute rounding).

Mountain recorded on the Soviet sheets and carried into GeoNames 614182 (dem 700 m) and Wikidata Q24684427. Adjacent to the separately-catalogued Gory Kala-Darasi massif — the Soviet map distinguished the single summit from the group.
Named hill above the village of Arkhiloskalo on the northern approach to the park, Wikidata Q24686091. Coordinate is low-precision (whole-arcminute).

1001.4 m summit immediately above Mount Elia, the highest point of the Dedoplistsqaro area, Wikidata Q12867621 with a Georgian Wikipedia article; GeoNames 612697 'Gora Nikoras-Tsikhe' gives 1001 m at 41.44188, 46.10958 with alternates Gora Nikoratsikhe / Nikoratsikho. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window; useful as an elevation control point.

Named peak/ridge visible to the south from the St Elias church above Eagle Gorge, together with the Taribana valley (per the official trekking-map description of route 1). OSM peak node at 41.2559, 46.0310, west of the park bounding box.

Long gorge running through the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve, named in the management plan as one of the valleys carrying shrubland and used by the return leg of the 'Land of the Hidden Water' route. Coordinate derived from the label position on the official trekking map via its UTM grid; the gorge is linear, so treat this as a point on its axis, accuracy about ±300 m.

Named seasonal stream/gorge draining east to the Alazani in the southern park. Plausibly the feature behind the 'Areulebi' ('eroded mountains caused by wind') that the Agency of Protected Areas lists among Vashlovani's attractions. OSM way 864945239 (centroid given).

The park's western and south-western river, OSM relation/12714402; known as Qabırlı / Qabırlı çayı on the Azerbaijani side. Coordinate is the centroid of in-park way/192218217; a further reach (way/944105850) centres at 41.0718, 46.4242, and the Iori Canal (way/1322467144) leaves it at 41.0802, 46.4396. The Iori plateau (ივრის ზეგანი) that the park sits on is named for it.

Forms the park's eastern and southern boundary and the Georgia-Azerbaijan frontier; OSM relation/12588097, Azerbaijani name Qanıx. Coordinate is the centroid of in-bbox way/125592959. A dedicated viewpoint 'Border Alazani River' (node/10081554153) sits at 41.1078, 46.6398. Holds about 20 fish species including Wels catfish, common carp, pike-perch, Caspian shemaya and shad; fly fishing permitted at designated spots near Mijniskure.

Saline watercourse; coordinate is the centroid of the main OSM river reach (way/285944554). CAUTION for the GIS layer: this hydronym is applied to at least ten separate OSM stream segments across the park (centroids from 41.115 to 41.299, lon 46.46 to 46.58), so it is a generic descriptive name rather than one river. Related interpretive point 'ლეკის (მლაშე) წყალი' (Lekis/salt water) at 41.1338, 46.5757.
Named saline water point/spring marked as a park interpretation node in the southern park near Bugha Moedani. OSM node 4424146494.
Named stream ('pigs' water') in the park's eastern Shavi Mta sector, OSM way/864966546; Nominatim returns it at 41.1783, 46.6366. Runs parallel to Areuli Khevi 3 km to its south.
Named seasonal stream in the south-central park, between Bugha Moedani and the Iori canal. OSM way 1067617513 (centroid given). Note the name resemblance to Qumuris Mta / 'Kumuro'.

Named valley (OSM node/8062272614, natural=valley) in the park's north-east near Sabatlo. 'Dzori' is the Armenian/Turkic loan for gorge, one of several Turkic-origin toponyms in this sector (cf. Bughdalu, Kadros Kutkhe).

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forests Natural Monument (Kaklis Kure / Walnut Bay)
sites.name_ka: ალაზნის ჭალის ტყის ბუნების ძეგლი / კაკლის ყურე
sites.description: IUCN-III natural monument established 2003: 204.4 ha of liana-draped relict floodplain forest in a peninsula-shaped bight of the Alazani, entered through a gap only 30-40 m wide, at 165 m a.s.l. The only place in Georgia with extensive natural stands of common walnut and common oak in floodplain forest; 1 km of trail takes about an hour. Official coordinate N41 21.548 E46 39.235 = 41.35913, 46.65392; OSM's Kaklis Kure locality node is 41.36568, 46.65535. English Wikipedia's 41.69917, 46.06444 for this monument is wrong (that point is far up the Alazani valley) - do not use it.

Semi-desert lowland at the extreme south-east of the Iori Plateau, the lowest ground of the Dedoplistskaro Biosphere Reserve at about 90 m; habitat for hundreds of reintroduced goitered gazelle, and the route by which Queen Ketevan was taken out of Georgia. Two Wikidata items: Q12864103 at 41.15, 46.3833 and Q55703380 ('Eldaris Dablobi', plain, 216 m) at 41.2, 46.31667.

The plateau between the Kura and Alazani rivers, transected by the Iori, 200-900 m, predominantly chernozem, largely steppe; Vashlovani occupies its south-eastern end. Wikipedia's coordinate (41.4155, 45.8775) is the plateau centroid, well north-west of the park.

Salt lake at 775 m near the village of Samreklo, visible to the east from the St Elias church above Eagle Gorge (named in the official route-1 description). Wikidata Q24687078; OSM lake at 41.4405, 46.1477. North-west of the park bounding box.

Lake in the Taribana valley, the area named to the south from the St Elias church in the official route description; the Taribana-Chachuna-Eldari track runs from here into the reserve country. West of the park bounding box (OSM natural=water).

Reservoir on the Iori below Dali Mountain, the halfway point of the official Takhti-Tepa route (35 km from the visitor centre) and the water body the Chachuna Managed Reserve was created to protect. Well west of the park bounding box; the only lat/lon found is from a detailed 4x4 field itinerary.

Artificial lake on the northern park approach by Kasristskali village, tagged in OSM as a camp site named 'Shiraqi Lake'; a cluster of four OSM water polygons sits immediately around it at 41.29514-41.29934 / 46.45633-46.45927. One of the few standing-water bodies inside the park bounding box and a prime Sentinel-2 cross-check target.

sites.name_en: Eldar Shami (Eldar Pine) State Nature Reserve
sites.description: Strict reserve protecting the relict Eldar pine (Pinus eldarica) stand in the Eldari lowland on the Iori, immediately south-west of Vashlovani. Wikidata Q4186734 at 41.172436, 46.216831; a second item (Q21982706, 'Eldar Şamı Qoruğ', 335 m) sits at 41.183889, 46.175278.

The park's southern outpost on the bank of the Alazani right at the Azerbaijan border: ranger station, bungalows, tent pitches, picnic areas and the park's designated fly-fishing water, reached by descending from the Usakhelo viewpoint. OSM locality node 760262846 at 41.1121, 46.64827; visitor-centre/bungalow node 1182746361 at 41.11175, 46.6462; park info node 4424085391 at 41.1111, 46.6467; a field itinerary gives 41.1111-41.1117, 46.6462-46.6467. Visitors must register in advance for this boundary zone.
The park's interior accommodation node (bungalows and tent ground) referred to in the official routes as the 'central bungalows'. OSM way 1322451821, tagged tourism=hostel.

Ranger post and picnic/parking area at the foot of the Shavi Mta massif, directly below the Zilcha summit and at the start of the trail to the convent ruins. OSM node 4424146593 at 41.2712, 46.62858, with a parking/picnic node at 41.26449, 46.63466; independently recorded at 41.2711, 46.6285 by a field itinerary.

Main (central) entrance to Vashlovani National Park, about 50 km from the Dedoplistsqaro visitor centre; all the eastern routes (Mijniskure, Shavi Mta, Imedi Gorge) start here, and it carries the first major overlook towards the reservoir and the Azerbaijan border. Coordinate from a detailed 4x4/field itinerary only - no official source publishes it.

Ranger station serving the Kaklis Kure / Alazani Floodplain Forests Natural Monument at the park's north-eastern corner, 60 km from the visitor centre. Coordinate from a field itinerary (41.3536, 46.6502); it lies ~700 m from the official monument coordinate.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani Protected Areas Visitor Centre, Dedoplistsqaro
sites.description: Administration and visitor centre at 5 Baratashvili St, Dedoplistsqaro, 130 km (about 2 h) from Tbilisi; also the hotel, tent-rental point and the building where the excavated Southern elephant bones are kept. Advance contact is required before using the trails, and boundary-zone permits (Mijniskure, Takhti-Tepa, Kaklis Kure) are issued here. Coordinate from a field itinerary.

sites.name_en: Georgian Border Police checkpoint (Iori / southern park)
sites.description: Border Police checkpoint mapped inside the southern park near the Iori canal; identity documents must be carried throughout the park. OSM way 998796932 at 41.10277, 46.47776. A separate border guard post on the Pantishara-Mijniskure axis is recorded at 41.1390, 46.5798 by a field itinerary.

5th-century city-fortress attributed to King Vakhtang Gorgasali on a steep isolated rock 3-4 km from Dedoplistsqaro, controlling the plateaus along the Alazani and Iori; chronicles call it the 'impregnable fortress' and Mihaly Zichy used it as the model for Kajeti Castle when illustrating The Knight in the Panther's Skin. Reached through a tree-tunnel road with a picnic area below. Wikidata Q13564048 gives 41°29'11.26"N 46°8'12.59"E = 41.48646, 46.13683, matching the OSM attraction node at 41.48606, 46.13578. Outside the park bounding box to the north-west. A field itinerary's 41.4729, 46.0854 appears to point at Khornabuji village instead.

sites.name_en: St Elias Mountain and Church (Elia / Tezbiteli)
sites.description: Limestone crag ~3 km from Dedoplistsqaro carrying a 5th-7th century church (built 6th c., restored 2008) reached by stairs and a trail about 45-60 m up the rock; the panorama takes in Lake Kochebi and the Shiraki plain east, and the Taribana valley and Kotsakhura ridge south. Third stop on the official Eagle Gorge route. Coordinate (41.4417, 46.1088) from a field itinerary only.

sites.name_en: Nazarlebi Early Iron Age Sanctuary and Settlement
sites.description: Mapped Early Iron Age sanctuary and settlement on the Iori-plateau rim north-west of the park, OSM way 643093870.

Ruined town site in the south-central park, OSM node 8927317168. An associated iron-smelting workshop ruin is mapped at 41.1576, 46.41806 (node 8927317169) and a settlement ruin near Mijnis Kure at 41.06184, 46.50305 (node 8927317167).

Last village before the park on the northern approach (Wikidata Q12865640, 500 m; OSM node 429443348), where the tracks divide towards Pantishara/Alesilebi, Vashlovani and Mijniskure and where the Didi Shiraki turnoff lies. Has a public school and town hall.

Abandoned Soviet military airfield on the Shiraki plain with surviving runways and hangars, passed on the drive in from Kasristskali. Wikidata Q6047327 gives 41.37954, 46.36733 at 547 m; OSM maps the brownfield area at 41.4174, 46.42142 and the military airfield polygon at 41.37852, 46.37436.

FLAGGED: lon 45.844 is outside the supplied park bbox, but the coordinate is authoritative, not a guess — it is the Agency of Protected Areas' own GPX waypoint (550 m), matching APA's UTM38N 570695/4566331, Wikidata Q12869613 (41.245683/45.843617) and OSM node 3578395922 to within ~130 m; the monument is simply a separate 9.7 ha unit of the Vashlovani Protected Areas complex, ~40 km WSW of the national park, south of Dalis Mta reservoir beside Chachuna Managed Reserve. A permanently active group of cold pseudo-volcanic (exo-volcanic) craters built of sandstone and clay: largest crater 3.5–4 m across, smaller gryphons and open vents 20 cm–1.5 m high, continuously extruding grey-blue clay slurry, oil and gas that drains downslope into ravines. Declared 2003, IUCN category III; 0.5 km walking path (~30 min), ~37 km of gravel/dirt road from Dedoplistsqaro, permit and border-police registration required; summit flora is halophytic (Kalidium caspicum, Suaeda sp., Petrosimonia brachiata, Limonium meyeri). Elevation is reported inconsistently as 541 m, 550 m and 620 m.

FLAGGED as outside the supplied park bbox (lon 45.733, Sighnaghi municipality, on the Iormuganlo–Taribana track) — reported because it is a third, essentially undocumented bubbling mud-volcano locality of the Iori plateau and the only one I found that is not already in the tourist literature. The Georgian name means 'the bubblers'. Evidence is mapping-platform only (OSM attraction node, confirmed through Nominatim); no agency, scientific or news source for it was located, so its size, activity and relation to the Kila-Kupra / Takhti-Tepa structures are unknown.

The park's signature badlands and its most important geosite: exhumed marine clay-sandstone strata eroded by wind and water into 'sharpened' walls 59–70 m high fronting a dense network of miniature clay ridges and ravines, widely nicknamed Georgian Mars. Corals, shells and fossilised crustaceans weather out of the walls, marking an old Sarmatian sea floor; griffon, Egyptian and black vultures nest on the faces. Coordinate is the mapped Alesilebi overlook (OSM 'ალესილების ხედი'); a second official overlook stands at 41.223614/46.406156 and the feature extends along the Kasristskali–Pantishara–Alesilebi track.

Side gorge at 371 m asl immediately NE of Pantishara, a network of steep eroded cliffs and ravines carved into the same Neogene clastics; million-year-old molluscs and vertebrate bone weather out of its walls. Georgian Wikipedia gives Datvis Khevi as a boundary of the strict reserve. APA picnic area and trailhead at 41.237456/46.364163; OSM information point at 41.23769/46.36554.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani fossil vertebrate locality ("fossil elephant bone finding place")
sites.description: Official on-trail palaeontological attraction above Bear Gorge; coordinate from the APA GPX (OSM agrees at 41.24553/46.36866). Peer-reviewed correction worth carrying into the GIS: Bukhsianidze & Koiava (2018, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 63:441–461) place the 'Vashlovani site' in the Shiraki Formation, late Miocene Turolian MN12 (upper age ~7 Ma), and state the collection contains only Gomphotheriidae indet. and Microstonyx major — the on-site attribution to the southern elephant Mammuthus meridionalis is explicitly erroneous, as are the popular 'dinosaur and mammoth bone' claims repeated by travel sites.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani measured stratigraphic section (Forte et al. 2015a reference section)
sites.description: A ~1475 m thick reference section through the Mio-Pliocene fill of the Kura Basin exposed in the Vashlovani area and divided into five units; it preserves the westernmost exposures of the Productive Series in the basin (5.35–2.95 Ma; massive cobble-to-boulder conglomerate interpreted as braid-plain / alluvial-fan), overlain by ~480 m of Akchagylian silt and claystone with fine–medium sandstone interbeds (meandering fluvial with periodic brackish lacustrine inundation). Sarmatian and Meotian–Pontian strata are exposed at Vashlovani and in the neighbouring Didi Shiraki piggyback basin because the shallow Kura fold-thrust-belt detachment soles at ~8 km here within the Upper Sarmatian; the regional detachment horizon itself is the Oligocene Maykopian gypsum-and-clay unit. No coordinate is published in the source fetched — the section-location table is rendered as figure art.

sites.name_en: Chachuna fossil locality (Akhtakhta-tapa and Djighati ranges)
sites.description: Late Miocene vertebrate locality in the marine Khersonian and the continental Eldari Formation (early Turolian, MN11) on the right bank of the Iori on the Akhtakhta-tapa (Akhtatapa) and Djighati (Kanly) ranges, Dedoplistsqaro district — immediately SW of the national park, in or beside Chachuna Managed Reserve. Discovered by V. M. Chkhikvadze in 2000; three rich bone concentrations known, with Choerolophodon sp., Hipparion sp., Aceratheriinae, Microstonyx major, Procapreolus, giraffids, boselaphines, trionychid turtles and Testudo. No coordinate published; the range names Akhtatapa/Djighati/Kanly return nothing in OSM or Nominatim, so this site cannot yet be pinned.

FLAGGED: lon 46.031 is outside the supplied park bbox (~25 km W of it) and the coordinate is DERIVED — it is the mapped Kotsakhura summit (564 m), i.e. the range, not the excavation. Bukhsianidze & Koiava (2018) place the Kotsakhuri site on the southern foothills of the Kotsakhuri range on the left bank of the Iori, Dedoplistsqaro district, in undivided Akchagylian–Apsheronian deposits (Early Pleistocene, middle Villafranchian MN17), with Mammuthus cf. meridionalis, Equus stenonis, Stephanorhinus cf. etruscus, Paracamelus sp., Leptobos, Croizetoceros and Struthio cf. transcaucasicus. A second mapped benchmark, 'მ.კოწახური, 354', sits at 41.232480/46.003560 on the Taribana–Chachuna–Eldari track.

FLAGGED as outside the park: a late Miocene Shiraki Formation site (early–middle Turolian, MN11–MN12) on the southern slope of Pirukugma Mountain, right bank of the Iori, Sighnaghi district, discovered by Trubikhin in the 1980s. Included because it exposes the same Shiraki Formation that yields the Vashlovani fossils, giving regional age control: Ergilemys natadzei, Adcrocuta eximia, Simocyon primigenius, Felis attica, Gomphotheriidae, Hipparion ex gr. elegans. No coordinate published and Pirukugma is absent from OSM/Nominatim.

FLAGGED as outside the supplied park bbox (lon 46.097). Two mapped cave entrances in the Eagle Gorge limestone — OSM nodes 12269156028 (41.489313/46.096888) and 12770911068 (41.490646/46.099138) — the concrete expression of the karst caves cited in descriptions of the protected areas. Both are unnamed in every source found and no speleological publication for them was located, so length, genesis and accessibility are unknown.

The Iori forms the park's south-western limit and its incised valley is the master drainage of the Iori plateau badlands, so nearly every geological site of the region is located by reference to its right or left bank: the Takhti-Tepa monument and the Chachuna and Dzedzvtakhevi fossil beds on the right bank, the Kotsakhuri beds on the left bank, and Dalis Mta reservoir impounding the river itself. The first fossil vertebrates of the region were reported from the Iori valley by Riabinin in 1913. No single published point coordinate; should be carried as a line feature, not a pin.

FLAGGED as outside the supplied park bbox (lon 45.891), but included because it is the universal locating landmark for the mud volcanoes — every source describes Takhti-Tepa as lying 'south / south-west of the Dali water reservoir', ~4.5 km SSW of this point. A man-made reservoir on the Iori at 257 m asl inside Chachuna Managed Reserve, with a border-police checkpoint at 41.278977/45.833334. IMPORTANT CROSS-REFERENCE ERROR: the coordinate pair 41.278998/45.891159, published by georgiantravelguide on a page titled 'Takhti Tepha and Kilakupra mud Volcanoes', is this reservoir and not a mud volcano.

FLAGGED as outside the supplied park bbox (lon 45.897). Mapped 763 m survey/viewpoint benchmark on the Takhti-Tepa ridge, ~7 km SSE of the mud craters — APA describes the monument as formed 'in proximity of the Takhti-Tepha mountain range', so this fixes the range the Natural Monument is named after. Reported because the 763 m crest, against the 541–620 m crater field, constrains the local relief the diapiric structure has to breach.

sites.name_en: Devebis Gadasakhedi (Giants' Viewpoint) over the canyons
sites.description: Mapped overlook, tagged in OSM as 'viewpoint canyons', onto the badland canyon system in the south-east of the reserve where the eroded clay ridges drop to the Alazani. A geomorphology observation pin over the lowest part of the park's relief; a border-Alazani viewpoint sits at 41.10778/46.63978 and a further overlook at 41.13245/46.65705.

Official APA GPX waypoint 'Scenic Viewpoint' on trail 2, the agency-sanctioned overlook onto the Alesilebi clay walls and the Pantishara canyon system; independently mapped as an OSM viewpoint at 41.22341/46.40609 (the figure circulating in travel write-ups as 'Pantishara Viewpoint, 41.2234/46.4061'). The Vashlovani Reserve ranger station and picnic area stand 1.5 km SSW at 41.215430/46.433378 and 41.215412/46.433883 (583 m).

Highest mapped summit inside the park at 845 m (prominence 217 m; the park maximum is usually quoted as 858 m), on the divide between the Shiraki plateau and the Kumuro side. It marks the top of the Neogene clastic pile the whole badland landscape is being cut into, against a park low point of 78–99 m on the Alazani.

Low open flat at 259 m in the south of the park, an APA trailhead with ranger station at 41.126266/46.538402 (OSM viewpoint at 41.12431/46.53801); the transition zone from badland relief to young Alazani alluvial ground. The park's central entrance and ranger post lie up-slope at 41.225408/46.533039 (397 m).

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forest (Kaklis Kure) Natural Monument
