sites.description: 204.4 ha Natural Monument declared in 2003 on an Alazani meander peninsula at 165 m asl — the youngest, lowest and purely alluvial ground of the Vashlovani complex and the geological counterpart of the upland badlands, carrying relict walnut, ash, oak and elm gallery forest. Coordinate from the APA GPX; ranger station at 41.359328/46.650121 and a border-police post at 41.337187/46.649278 (219 m).

sites.name_en: Unnamed spring, Shiraki plateau edge near Kasristskali
sites.description: OSM-mapped spring (node 12248692801) on the plateau NE of Pantishara, close to the Kasristskali road waypoint at 41.289768/46.459571 (521 m). Reported under the salt/mineral-spring part of this research angle, with an explicit caveat: the node carries no water-quality, salinity or mineral tags and no publication describes it, so any classification as a mineral or salt spring would be unsupported.

OSM-mapped spring (node 13270249903) in the plateau interior of the park; like the Kasristskali spring it has no chemistry tags, so it is a located water point rather than a verified mineral spring. A third node at 41.336291/46.545960 is tagged in OSM with a fixme warning that it may be a leaking water pipe rather than a spring and should not be published as a natural feature without ground-truthing; a named drinking spring, Mazovkis Tsqali (მაზოვკის წყალი), lies well outside the park at 41.477769/46.094948 near Eagle Gorge.

sites.name_en: Mamachai and Eshmaki gorges (western boundary gorges of Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve)
sites.description: Georgian Wikipedia's boundary definition of the 9,962 ha Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve names the Mamachais-khevi and Eshmakis-khevi ('Devil's gorge') watershed divide as its western limit, with the Didis Shdilis / Dibis ridge and the southern slopes of the Pantishara massif to the south and the Kumuro plain to the east. Reported as named-but-unlocated canyon features: no coordinate was found, neither name resolves in OSM or Nominatim, and the transliterations are uncertain, so these are leads for further mapping rather than pinnable sites.

Named as the eastern boundary of Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve in the Georgian-language description of the reserve, i.e. the low plain between the badland uplands and the Alazani. No coordinate found: the name returns nothing in OSM or Nominatim, and the only plausible cognate is a 'Gora Komroy' (370 m) listed among the park's peaks by PeakVisor, which I could not confirm as the same feature.

IUCN Category Ia strict reserve of 10,143 ha (4,032 ha forest) established 1935 on the Shiraki range and the Georgian bank of the Alazani, 300-600 m. Protects the park's core pistachio-juniper arid light woodland (Pistacia mutica, Juniperus foetidissima/polycarpos/oxycedrus) plus Celtis, wild pear, pomegranate, mahaleb cherry and paliurus. Historic faunal records include striped hyena, leopard, wolf, brown bear, griffon vulture; 1950-1970 hyena records came 'mostly in remote gorges of the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve'. Closed to general visitors.

sites.name_en: Nugzar Zazanashvili Samukhi Multipurpose Use Protected Area (Samukhi / Eldari steppe)
sites.description: 13,273 ha IUCN Category VI area approved by Parliament in 2022, in force 1 Jan 2023 — Georgia's first Category VI PA, created specifically to hold the reintroduced goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) population. A wide strip of low salt steppe (EUNIS E6.2 Continental inland salt steppes, dominant vegetation here) between the NP and the Azerbaijan border. Also the main transboundary wintering site for Little Bustard in Georgia (roosting flocks up to ~1,000; coordinated surveys 2020-2024 recorded 27,000-28,000 in the wider region), with disturbance low because of militarised border control. Coordinate is the eBird hotspot centroid (288 records, 94 species) recording griffon, cinereous and Egyptian vulture, short-toed snake eagle and black francolin.

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forests Natural Monument (Kakliskure tugay forest)
sites.description: 204.4 ha tugay-type riparian floodplain forest on the right bank of the Alazani, SW of village Pirosmani, 165 m a.s.l.; the park's flagship riparian habitat. Dense liana cover over perennial walnut, ash, pedunculate oak, elm, poplar and wild pomegranate. Pheasant (Phasianus colchicus) strongholds are in the Alazani groves; black stork forages here. Reached via the Kakliskure-Alaznis Chala route, 56 km from Dedoplistsqaro; 1 km foot trail takes ~1 hour. Coordinate converted from the official UTM 38N value (X 638346, Y 4580257) and cross-checked against nationalparks.ge (N41 21.548 E46 39.235) and the eBird hotspot 'Alazani Floodplain Natural Monument' (41.35334, 46.65000).

sites.name_en: Artsivi (Eagle) Gorge Natural Monument — griffon vulture colony
sites.description: THE key documented vulture breeding site of the Vashlovani Protected Areas: a 1.74 km2 limestone canyon plus adjoining forest ~2 km from Dedoplistsqaro town. UNDP/CNF monitoring (Javakhishvili & Paposhvili, 2021-2023) counted 24 griffon vulture (Gyps fulvus) pairs in 2023 — 23 initiated nesting, 22 successful, 21 near-fledged juveniles, 91.3% breeding success; 3 Egyptian vulture (Neophron percnopterus) pairs, 2 successful, 2 fledglings; 5 black stork (Ciconia nigra) pairs, 2 successful, 4 fledglings, 40% nesting success. Gavashelishvili & Javakhishvili earlier found griffon colonies on the cliffs of Eagle Canyon, Khornabuji fortress and adjoining cliffs with 2 Egyptian vulture pairs; Shoshitaishvili (2020) found 4 black stork pairs on the same cliffs. Also breeding imperial, spotted, lesser spotted, steppe, booted and short-toed eagle, and peregrine. Observation decks installed. CONFIDENCE LOW ONLY BECAUSE the coordinate (lon 46.094) falls outside the supplied park bbox — the monument genuinely lies NW of the NP near Dedoplistsqaro. Coordinate is corroborated by two independent sources: Wikipedia decimal degrees and my conversion of apa/nationalparks.ge UTM 38N X 591747 Y 4593825 (= 41.49079, 46.09909).

sites.name_en: Khornabuji fortress cliffs — griffon / Egyptian vulture nesting cliffs
sites.description: 5th-century fortress on a limestone crag ~3-4 km north of Dedoplistsqaro. Gavashelishvili & Javakhishvili recorded Eurasian griffon nesting colonies on 'the cliffs of Eagle canyon, Khornabuji fortress and adjusting cliffs', the same cliffs holding 2 Egyptian vulture pairs, and Shoshitaishvili (2020) counted 4 black stork pairs across the Eagle canyon/Khornabuji cliff complex — i.e. this is treated in the literature as one continuous breeding population with Eagle Canyon. The UNDP 2023 survey deliberately examined surrounding cliffs outside the NM boundary for nests for that reason. CONFIDENCE LOW ONLY because lon 46.137 is outside the supplied bbox; coordinate is from Wikidata.

9.7 ha natural monument (1 ha of active crater field) on a sandstone/clay plain south of the Dali water reservoir at 620 m, part of Vashlovani Protected Areas. Constantly active mud craters and small vents erupting mud, oil and gas; the largest crater is 3.5-4 m across, with 'springs of different sizes with grey-blue bubbling clay'. 0.5 km pedestrian path; reached as a 110 km day trip from Dedoplistsqaro via Dali Mountain. CONFIDENCE LOW ONLY because lon 45.844 lies far west of the supplied bbox — the site is genuinely in the Chachuna/Iori sector of the protected-area complex, not in the NP. Coordinate corroborated twice: Wikipedia decimal degrees and my conversion of the apa/nationalparks.ge UTM 38N value X 570695 Y 4566331 (= 41.24530, 45.84372).

sites.name_en: Chachuna vulture supplementary feeding station and birdwatching hide
sites.description: SABUKO (Society for Nature Conservation, BirdLife partner) built and opened (27 Nov 2023) a supplementary feeding station for vultures ('vulture restaurant') plus a purpose-built birdwatching space for observing vultures in flight and at the carcass, a hikers' hub, a campsite and an eight-person eco-cottage on the Iori bank, inside Chachuna Managed Reserve. Built 2021-2022 with GEF Small Grants Programme, UNDP, the Agency of Protected Areas and the Endangered Landscapes & Seascapes 'Kakheti steppes' project. No coordinate published in any source I could reach.

sites.name_en: Samukhi artificial waterholes (solar-pumped gazelle water system)
sites.description: WWF Caucasus, with the Ministry of Environment, the Agency of Protected Areas and the Wildlife Adaptation Innovation Fund (WAIF/WWF-US), installed a solar power plant beside the Iori river channel feeding a 5 km pipeline to three reservoirs at different points inside the Nugzar Zazanashvili Samukhi Multipurpose Use Protected Area, to provide dry-season water for the reintroduced goitered gazelles. Part of a six-waterhole transboundary network (3,597-9,592 gallons each) shared with Azerbaijan's Gakh protected area. Critical dry-season wildlife water points in a landscape where the NP itself has almost no surface water. No coordinates published.

sites.name_en: Mijniskure ranger station and campsite (Alazani / Iori confluence tugay)
sites.description: The park's south-eastern outpost on the Alazani bank right against the Azerbaijan border: ranger station, bungalows, campsite and a well — reportedly the only water source inside Vashlovani NP, which makes it the de-facto dry-season wildlife water focus and the single most-birded spot in the park. Border-zone permit and ID registration required at the Vashlovani Protected Areas visitor centre. Xeno-canto 2025 recordings from here (41.1118, 46.6462) include Alectoris chukar, Sylvia mystacea (Menetries's warbler), Dendrocopos syriacus, Tachymarptis melba, Coturnix coturnix, Picus viridis. GBIF also holds semi-desert and wadi records labelled 'Mijniskure, semidesert' and 'Mijniskure road, wadi'.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani Nature Reserve (Mijniskure) — eBird hotspot / bird monitoring point
sites.description: The richest systematic bird-recording point in the park: 391 georeferenced eBird records covering 103 species reach GBIF from this hotspot (2007-2024), including cinereous vulture (Aegypius monachus), griffon vulture, Egyptian vulture and short-toed snake eagle. Functions as the standing monitoring station for the Mijniskure sector's semi-desert / tugay ecotone. Coordinate is the eBird hotspot centroid.

Working ranger post on the Kasristskali-Vashlovani track, the operational base for the Pantishara sector and the staging point for the Pantishara-Datviskhevi route. Rangers here run SMART-system GPS anti-poaching patrols and supported the gazelle pre-release enclosure. Doubles as a bird monitoring point: 42 eBird records / 30 species incl. cinereous vulture, griffon vulture and short-toed snake eagle; nearby iNaturalist and Xeno-canto records cluster at 41.2150-41.2145, 46.433-46.434.

sites.name_en: Pantishara Gorge and Valley — griffon vulture breeding cliffs
sites.description: Narrow canyon and dry riverbed between high cliffs, ~13 km SW of Kasristskali, the classic raptor and cliff-passerine site of the park. Breeding griffon vulture on the canyon walls plus Western rock nuthatch (Sitta neumayer), black-eared wheatear, chukar, rock bunting, rock sparrow, rufous-tailed scrub robin and blue rock thrush; Egyptian vulture recorded repeatedly (e.g. 41.23551/46.36434, May 2017). Relict pistachio and evergreen juniper on the ridges. Xeno-canto 2025 point 'Vashlovani reserve (western canyons)' at 41.23800/46.36540 yielded Monticola solitarius, Emberiza cia, Sitta neumayer, Sylvia crassirostris, Tachymarptis melba, Delichon urbicum. Herbarium vouchers of Pistacia atlantica/mutica come from the gorge's left side.

Side gorge off Pantishara with a marked walking trail (Pantishara - Datvis Khevi). Treated as one birding unit with Pantishara in eBird ('Pantishara & Bear Canyon, Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve', 41.23361-41.23572 / 46.36252-46.36486) with griffon and Egyptian vulture records. Also a palaeontological site: fossilised marine molluscs and an 87 cm southern-elephant shoulder blade are exposed in the gorge walls. Coordinate is the OSM trail information board; a GBIF locality 'Datviskhevi' sits at 41.23662/46.36910.

Wind-carved clay cliff formations 59-70 m high at the end of the Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi track, described as a favourite hangout/perching spot for eagles and griffon vultures and a feature of the Pantishara-Datviskhevi route. COORDINATE IS DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED: no source gives a point for Alesilebi itself; I averaged iNaturalist/eBird records whose locality string is the 'Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi' track (41.2355-41.2374 / 46.3644-46.3740), so the value is really the Pantishara end of that track and may be several km off the actual rocks. Treat as an approximate anchor only.

sites.name_en: 'City of Swallows' swallow nesting colony, Pantishara gorge
sites.description: A dense swallow (hirundine) breeding colony in the vertical clay precipices of the Pantishara gorge, named as a feature of the Pantishara-Datviskhevi route by the park authority and described in the park's nature account as 'Town of swallows' — swallow colonies in clay precipices. A discrete, nameable colonial-bird habitat site. No coordinate published; it lies within the Pantishara gorge (see that entry).

The park approach road from Kasristskali, one of the most productive raptor-watching transects in the reserve: 188 eBird records / 71 species reach GBIF (2013-2024), including cinereous vulture, griffon vulture, Egyptian vulture and short-toed snake eagle. Also the location of the former Institute of Botany experiment station near Kasris Tskali (herbarium Pistacia atlantica voucher at 41.28361/46.46833). Coordinate is the eBird hotspot centroid.

sites.name_en: Kasristskali (village and plains) — small-mammal survey locality
sites.description: Settlement and cultivated plain at the northern gateway to the park, the junction where one track runs SW to Pantishara and another SE to Mijniskure. A long-running rodent survey locality: GBIF's 'Rodent occurrence in Georgia' dataset holds records from 1939, 1984 and 1990 at 41.29050/46.46675 for Apodemus witherbyi, Cricetulus migratorius (grey dwarf hamster), Microtus arvalis, Microtus socialis, Mus macedonicus and Lepus europaeus, plus a 1939 record from 'Kasristskali, State farm Eldari'. eBird 'Kasristskali Plains' point at 41.25467/46.43146.

sites.name_en: Shiraki Valley (Shiraki steppe) — bustard and raptor wintering plain
sites.description: Large steppe/farmland plain north of the park, one of the five sites in SABUKO's coordinated 2020-2024 winter Little Bustard surveys (Tetrax tetrax used the valley in smaller numbers than Samukhi/Taribana; a poaching case with 16 killed birds was prosecuted in Dedoplistskaro municipality in 2016). Also a rich raptor site: 292 eBird records / 58 species incl. Egyptian vulture, short-toed snake eagle, imperial eagle and black francolin. Historic steppe rodent locality — 'Shiraki steppe' 41.38700/46.39400 (1978) with Meriones libycus and Mesocricetus brandti; 'Didi Shiraki' 41.38386/46.36029 (1984-2000) with Mesocricetus brandti, Apodemus witherbyi, Dryomys nitedula, Microtus socialis. Threatened by expanding olive and almond plantations and overgrazing.

Disused airfield on the Shiraki plain (OSM landuse=brownfield, 41.37852/46.37436) whose unploughed short-sward grassland is used as a discrete bird survey point — 12 eBird records / 12 species and iNaturalist records (41.38011/46.37653). Useful as an unimproved-steppe reference patch inside an increasingly ploughed/planted plain.

sites.name_en: Bugha Moedani plateau and goitered gazelle breeding enclosure
sites.description: Extensive grassland plateau in the south-central park, the single most important vegetation and ungulate-management site inside the NP. UNDP's 2021 pasture monitoring identifies Bugha Moedani and Kumuro as the main stands of Mediterraneo-Anatolian andropogonid grass steppe (EUNIS E1.4345) in the park, ~2,500 ha. NACRES's reintroduction plan places the ~5 ha goitered-gazelle pre-release/breeding enclosure on this grassland ('Boegi Moedani'), with Gumuru Maidani below it at the head of Gumuru valley, which forms the dispersal corridor to the Samukhi steppes. Enclosure vegetation is dominated by rank Bothriochloa ischaemum >1 m tall with heavy litter mats, judged suboptimal forage and in need of cutting/grazing/burning management. Of nine gazelles first released, all three collared animals were killed by predators within two months, prompting a change of release method and site. OSM tags a natural=plateau node here and a viewpoint at 41.12431/46.53801.

Valley on the eastern side of the reserve running down from Bugha Moedani; Gumuru Maidani lies below the gazelle enclosure at its head. NACRES identify it as the corridor connecting the Vashlovani release site to the adjoining Samukhi (Eldari) steppes and thence the wider Iori Plateau, i.e. the functional dispersal route for the reintroduced gazelle population. UNDP's pasture report spells it 'Kumuro' and lists it with Bugha Moedani as a core andropogonid grass-steppe stand; PeakVisor lists a 'Gora Komroy' (370 m) in the park, probably the same feature. No coordinate published under any spelling.

Interpretation/observation point on the Pantishara-Eldari track overlooking the Samukhi (Eldari) plain — the gazelle and Little Bustard core area. Nearby eBird units: 'Samukhi plains (Vashlovani Nature Reserve)' 41.18176/46.36076 with griffon and Egyptian vulture, and 'Northern Samukhi' 41.20027/46.33743. OSM tourism=information node.

Named eBird survey locality on the northern edge of the Samukhi salt steppe, recording black francolin (Francolinus francolinus) among other steppe species; sits between the Pantishara canyon system and the Samukhi gazelle range. Coordinate is the eBird locality centroid.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani NP East / Pantishara viewpoint raptor watchpoint
sites.description: Named eBird watchpoint pair on the ridge between the ranger station and the Pantishara canyon ('Vashlovani NP East' 41.22360/46.40611, 21 records, and 'Pantishara viewpoint' 41.22340/46.40602): repeated griffon vulture and Egyptian vulture observations, i.e. a usable vantage over the vulture flight lines out of the canyon. Corroborating iNaturalist cluster 'Pantishara-Vashlovani' at 41.22340/46.40992.

sites.name_en: Eldari steppe / Eldari plain — semi-desert rodent and lark community
sites.description: The park's classic semi-desert (Artemisia/Salsola) plain on the Pantishara-Eldari track and the best-sampled small-mammal site in the reserve: GBIF's Georgian rodent dataset holds 12 records here spanning 1939-2021 for Allactaga elater (small five-toed jerboa), Meriones libycus (Libyan jird), Microtus socialis, Mus macedonicus and Lepus europaeus — i.e. the prey base underpinning the lynx, hyena and raptor guild. A 2025 Xeno-canto point 'Vashlovani reserve (Eldari plain)' at 41.15860/46.40780 recorded Calandrella rufescens (lesser short-toed lark). Historic 2004 records from 'Eldar Sham reserve' list imperial eagle and black francolin.

sites.name_en: Zilcha Mountain (highest point of Vashlovani NP)
sites.description: The park's high point at 847 m (prominence 217 m) in the eastern block above the Alazani slope. A small-mammal survey locality: rodent records from 1939 and 2018 at 41.27733/46.61538 for Cricetulus migratorius, Meriones libycus, Microtus socialis, Mus macedonicus and Lepus europaeus. Coordinate is the OSM natural=peak node; the GBIF locality point lies ~2 km WSW, so the two sources bracket the summit area. (The task brief's 858 m park maximum is slightly higher than PeakVisor's 847 m for this summit.)

sites.name_en: Pistachio arid light woodland, Pantishara gorge left bank
sites.description: Vouchered stand of Pistacia atlantica/mutica arid light woodland: herbarium collections labelled 'East Georgia, Dedoplistskaro District. Vashlovani, Pantishara gorge. Left side of the gorge' (2006) carry this coordinate, with further 1999 vouchers from 'Vashlovani Reserve: Semi-desert, canyon wash' at 41.23750/46.38027 and 41.23888/46.38861. This is the westernmost well-documented pistachio stand in the reserve and one of the two arid light-woodland types (pistachio-dominated and juniper-dominated) the park was designated to protect.

sites.name_en: Pistachio light woodland stand, central Vashlovani reserve
sites.description: Historic vouchered pistachio open-woodland stand in the reserve interior — the specimen locality reads, in Russian, 'Eastern Georgia. Vashlovani reserve. Pistachio light woodland' (фисташковое редколесье), collected 1961. Plus further reserve-interior Pistacia vouchers at 41.18554/46.45157 (1958) and 41.17715-41.18221/46.46-46.55. Marks the historical extent of the pistachio 'redkolesye' formation in the core zone, useful as a baseline for stand-change analysis.

sites.name_en: Lekistskali Gorge and river (pistachio stand, hare/jird locality)
sites.description: Side gorge and seasonal river in the south-central reserve. A 2010 herbarium voucher of Pistacia atlantica is labelled 'Georgia:Kiziki:Dedoplistskaro:Kasristskali, Lekistskali Gorge' at this coordinate, and the Georgian rodent dataset has a 'Lekistskali river' locality at 41.16200/46.56350 with Lepus europaeus and Meriones libycus. Together they make this a documented pistachio-woodland / semi-desert small-mammal site away from the main tracks.

Named gorge in the reserve interior recorded as a small-mammal locality (Lepus europaeus, 1962) in GBIF's Georgian rodent dataset. Adjoins the Lekistskali and central pistachio-woodland localities; the sort of remote gorge in which mid-20th-century striped hyena records were concentrated. No other source found for the name — the transliteration may vary (Chigho-elt-khevi).

Xeno-canto 2025 sound-recording station in the eastern reserve near the Alazani slope, 9 recordings: Aegithalos caudatus, Dendrocopos syriacus, Emberiza cia, Oenanthe hispanica, Parus major, Sitta neumayer, Sylvia crassirostris, Sylvia curruca — a woodland/scrub assemblage distinct from the western canyons. Useful as a fixed acoustic-monitoring point.

Named locality on the Alazani side of the park, start of the 'Takhis tskali - Shavi mta' track that climbs into the eastern massif. GBIF's rodent dataset has a Takhistskali locality (Lepus europaeus, 1962) at 41.17000/46.64700, and iNaturalist records a 'Takhis tskali-Shavi mta' cluster at 41.22841/46.57856. OSM records it as place=locality (i.e. no longer an inhabited village).

Named ridge in the western badlands recorded as a recent (2018 and 2021) locality for Meriones libycus, the Libyan jird, in GBIF's Georgian rodent dataset — i.e. an active semi-desert small-mammal monitoring point on the Iori side of the park. No other source found for the name.

Named low-mountain area in the western part of the reserve, recorded as a 2018 Mus macedonicus locality in GBIF's Georgian rodent dataset. Sits within the badlands belt between Patara Shiraki and the Pantishara canyon system. Single-source name.

Steppe/farmland tract on the park's north-western approach, sampled for rodents in 2018 and 2021 (Mus macedonicus, Mus musculus at this point; Meriones libycus at the adjacent 'Patara Shiraki' locality 41.28610/46.32057). OSM maps Patara Shiraki farmland polygons at 41.28113/46.31812 and 41.26542/46.44001, so the name covers a broad cultivated block rather than a point.

Named eBird survey locality in the fields east of the park towards the Alazani, with griffon vulture and short-toed snake eagle records (2024) — relevant as vulture foraging habitat (griffon breeding-site selection in the Caucasus correlates positively with open area and dead-livestock biomass within 20 km, per Gavashelishvili & McGrady). GBIF's rodent dataset also has a 'Sabatlo' locality (Microtus socialis, 2000) further north at 41.32800/46.66900, so the name spans a larger farmed area.

Steppe locality on the Iori side of the protected-area complex, sampled 2000-2020 for Lepus europaeus, Meriones libycus and Scarturus williamsi (Williams's jerboa) — a genuinely arid-adapted rodent assemblage. Marks the transition from the Vashlovani badlands to the Iori Plateau grasslands that NACRES identified as excellent gazelle habitat.

Riparian gallery/tugay forest strip along the Iori, recorded as a named small-mammal locality ('Iori river riparian forest', Lepus europaeus) in GBIF's Georgian rodent dataset. The Iori tugay is one of the two riparian forest systems (with the Alazani) that BirdLife's Iori Region IBA account lists as a defining habitat, and striped hyena in Georgia is specifically associated with 'the riparian forests of Iori and Alazani'. Vegetation elsewhere in the Iori tugay comprises Populus, Tamarix bush communities, reeds, long-stalk oak and white willow.

sites.name_en: Kotsakhura ridge (Kotsakhura Emerald Network Site) — lynx and hyena stronghold
sites.description: Ridge between the Vashlovani badlands and Chachuna, designated as the Kotsakhura Emerald Network Site. Ecologically important on three counts: (1) UNDP's 2022 Eurasian lynx camera-trap census found lynx ONLY on the left side of the Iori, on Kotsakhura ridge, and unexpectedly could not detect lynx in the badlands / right bank of the Iori in Chachuna where they were last photographed in 2012 — a possible spatial shift of the population; (2) striped hyena was 'recently spotted on the Iori Plateau near the Kotsakhuri Mountain Range'; (3) one of the five coordinated Little Bustard winter survey sites and one of the three key wintering areas in Georgia. CONFIDENCE LOW: the OSM natural=peak coordinate (lon 46.031) lies west of the supplied bbox, correctly so — the ridge is outside the NP.

Unprotected valley in Dedoplistskaro municipality, one of the three key Little Bustard wintering areas in Georgia alongside Samukhi and Kotsakhura; the largest flock in the 9 December 2023 independent survey was 260 birds here. Actively being lost to olive plantation conversion (photographed 2024) and pasture degradation, which fragments the wintering range and concentrates flocks into isolated, poaching-exposed patches. NO COORDINATE REPORTED: the only OSM match is a point on the long 'Taribana-Chachuna-Eldari' road (41.19669/46.22563) which is not the valley itself, so I have omitted lat/lon rather than publish a misleading one.

Plain named in UNDP's pasture monitoring as the slope target of the park's only Mediterranean feathergrass steppe stand ('confined to the Shavi Mta area on the slopes towards Dilicha plain'). Coordinate is the OSM 'Farmer's House in Vashlovani (Dilicha)' guest house on the Kasristskali-Mijniskure road, which is the only georeferenced use of the name I could find — so it anchors the name, not the plain's centroid.

Visitor centre / accommodation node inside the park on the Kasristskali-Mijniskure road (OSM tourism=hostel, name 'Vashlovani Visitor Center'). Distinct from the Vashlovani Protected Areas Administration in Dedoplistsqaro town (Baratashvili str. 5, tel +995 577 10 18 49), where border-zone permits for Mijniskure and the reserve must be obtained and where APA supplies the visitor statistics used in the vulture disturbance analysis. Single-source (OSM), hence medium confidence.

sites.name_en: Caucasian leopard 'Noah' monitoring area, Vashlovani Protected Areas
sites.description: The only documented live Caucasian (Persian) leopard in Georgia in modern times. NACRES found its tracks in Vashlovani in 2003 — the first Caucasian leopard track recorded — then photographed it by camera trap in 2004 and monitored the young male by tracking and camera trapping for nearly five years; the last footprints in the Vashlovani Protected Areas were found in 2009. Vashlovani remains the reference site for leopard presence in Georgia. NACRES publish no coordinates or station locations for the tracking/camera-trap effort.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani / Chachuna Eurasian lynx camera-trap grid (2022 census)
sites.description: UNDP/NACRES winter-spring 2022 Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx) population census: 36 camera-trap sites, two cameras per site — 22 pairs in Vashlovani and 14 in Chachuna Managed Reserve, plus ~10 extra single cameras on trails actively used by large mammals (station IDs recoverable from the report include Lynx 01, Lynx 11, Lynx 16, Lynx 22, Lynx 23, Lynx 26). Lynx was selected as a priority monitoring indicator for Vashlovani; in this semi-arid system it depends on small prey (hare, pheasant, chukar). Results: lynx detected only on the left bank of the Iori on Kotsakhura ridge, none in the badlands or right bank, where they were last photographed in 2012. Unregulated winter/early-spring grazing flagged as disturbance to prey. THE STATION COORDINATES ARE NOT RECOVERABLE: 'Appendix 3. Camera trap locations' exists but is image-only in the published PDF.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani NP and Samukhi grassland monitoring plot network (2021)
sites.description: Permanent vegetation monitoring network: 43 of 93 national sample plots were placed in Vashlovani NP and the Samukhi plains during March-September 2021, distributed across all habitat types of interest, each a 10x10 m quadrat with corners marked by iron nails so they can be relocated with a metal detector plus stored coordinates at the next assessment. Four habitat classes were mapped (EUNIS): E1.4345 Mediterraneo-Anatolian andropogonid grass steppe (76%), E6.2 Continental inland salt steppes (20%, dominant in Samukhi), E1.432 Mediterranean feathergrass steppes (2%, Shavi Mta only), F3.2471 Ponto-Sarmatic steppe brush (2%). Grasslands were assessed as being in moderate condition overall; salt steppe in Samukhi is singled out for special monitoring and grazing management because of the gazelles. PLOT COORDINATES NOT PUBLISHED: 'Appendix 1: Locations of sample plots' is map images, and the Appendix 2 data table only prints 24 Javakheti/Tabatskuri rows.

sites.name_en: Iori Region Important Bird and Biodiversity Area
sites.description: BirdLife-designated IBA of 239,374 ha, 100-900 m, encompassing Vashlovani and the surrounding Iori basin: hilly country with naturally eroded low ridges and many gorges, the driest climate in Georgia, with steppe and savanna-like landscapes, arid woodlands and semi-deserts and an abundance of relict and endemic plants. Vegetation listed as relict Bothriochloa and Stipa steppes, scattered savanna-like and Juniperus arid woodlands, Artemisia/Salsola semi-desert, and riparian forest along the Iori and Alazani. Qualifies chiefly for breeding and wintering birds of prey, with 25 raptor species recorded. CONFIDENCE LOW: the published IBA centre (46.0 E) falls outside the supplied park bbox because the IBA is an order of magnitude larger than the NP; the site polygon does contain the park.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani Protected Areas Visitor Centre & Administration (Dedoplistsqaro)
sites.description: Mandatory first stop: 5 Baratashvili St, Dedoplistsqaro. All park entry is registered here, the border-zone referral letter is issued here, paper maps (3 GEL) and rental tents are sold here, and bungalows must be booked here. Hours reported as weekdays 10:00-18:00 (APA/overlando) or daily 09:00-18:00 (nationalparks.ge), with permit applications accepted no later than 16:00; tel +995 577 10 18 49. Coordinate lies west of the park bounding box because the town itself is outside the park.

sites.name_en: Border Police station, Dedoplistsqaro (border-zone permit issue point)
sites.description: Second stop after the Visitor Centre, about a 5-minute drive away. Officers log passport details and issue the stamped free Border Zone Permit required for Mijniskure, Kaklis Kure and Takhti-Tepa; the whole two-office process takes under an hour. Advance application (4+ working days, Form N1 plus passport photo and vehicle documents) is possible by email to gpb@mia.gov.ge. Coordinate is west of the park bbox because the office is in the town.

sites.name_en: Vashlovani central ranger station / horse ranch (central park entrance)
sites.description: The park's main in-field ranger station and the 'central entrance' referenced by official route descriptions, roughly 50 km from the Dedoplistsqaro Visitor Centre on the Kasristskali-Vashlovani track. OSM maps a campsite, picnic site, toilets, viewpoint, information board ('Flora') and a horse-riding base at this node; two independent route pages publish essentially this coordinate as their second waypoint (41.215448/46.433002 and 41.215722/46.43341). Cottages and route information are available here, and a trail to the ancient pistachio grove starts nearby.

sites.name_en: Mijniskure bungalow camp, visitor shelter and Alazani fishing base
sites.description: The park's far south-eastern terminus on the Alazani floodplain at the Azerbaijan border, and the end point of official routes 5, 6 and 8. OSM maps a visitor-centre/hostel building plus seven chalets (bungalows), toilets, guideposts and a 'Floodplain Forest' information board in a tight cluster at 41.1111-41.1120 N, 46.6456-46.6473 E; a route page publishes the waypoint as 41.111092/46.646635. Tent camping, picnic areas and designated fly fishing are permitted; a well here is repeatedly described as the only reliable water source inside the park. Reaching it requires the border permit and a final steep narrow canyon descent.

A second bungalow cluster deep inside the park on the Karistskali-Mijniskure track, mapped in OSM as a hostel plus nine chalets at 41.1595-41.1601 N, 46.5659-46.5673 E, with a ford immediately north at 41.159975/46.568421. Quoted at 100 GEL per bungalow with hot-water showers and evening-only electricity; used as the overnight stop on official route 7 (Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta). Water here is described as technical (non-drinking).

sites.name_en: Pantishara / Datvis Khevi campsite and picnic area
sites.description: Official campsite at the mouth of Bear Gorge, reached after the Pantishara canyon descent. OSM maps a campsite, picnic site, toilets, shelter, an information board ('The Fossilized World of Vashlovani') and the trailhead map 'Pantishara - Datvis Khevi (Bear Gorge) Trail' at 41.2373/46.3655. This is the standard day-trip lunch and overnight point on official route 2.

Side canyon off Pantishara (OSM node/11792582004, tourism=attraction; a second info node დათვის ხევი at 41.2377, 46.3655). Its walls expose fossilised woody plants and seashells; an interpretive board 'The Fossilized World of Vashlovani' and a trail map board stand at the trailhead, with a shelter, campsite and picnic site at 41.2377-41.2378, 46.3651.

sites.name_en: End of car way (lower Pantishara barrier)
sites.description: OSM information node explicitly marking where the vehicle track ends on the Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi road and walking begins. Directly useful for answering 'where can a car not go' — this is the signed limit of driving in the Pantishara/Bear Gorge arm.

sites.name_en: End of car way (upper Alesilebi barrier)
sites.description: Second signed end-of-vehicle-track node about 1 km north-east of the first, above the Bear Gorge campsite. Beyond it the Alesilebi badlands and fossil sites are foot-only.

OSM attraction node marking where Southern elephant (Archidiskodon) bones were excavated on the Datvis Khevi trail; the official map confirms the find and that the bones are now kept at the Dedoplistsqaro administration building. Foot access only, beyond the end-of-car-way nodes.

Signed viewpoint over the 'razor-sharp' eroded clay pillars and pyramids that the park is known for, on the Pantishara arm of the route network. A second Pantishara-valley interpretation point sits at 41.227870/46.351116.

428 m summit with a built viewing platform, the classic badlands panorama and the last high point before the track drops to Mijniskure. Named as a main attraction of official routes 5 and 6 and used as the mid-route stop on most published one-day loops.

Signed canyon overlook on the Mijniskure road with an adjacent 'Canyons' interpretation board (41.127201/46.607122) and pit toilets (41.127379/46.606423) — one of only a handful of built facilities on the southern arm of the network.

Plateau (mapped separately at 41.132472/46.538776) and signed viewpoint on the Pantishara-Eldari track, giving the semi-desert panorama toward the snow-capped Caucasus. Start point of official route 7 (Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta, 200 km, 2 days). A 'Semi-Desert' interpretation board stands at 41.132307/46.530411.
Signed viewpoint in the park interior between the central ranger station and the Karistskali-Mijniskure track. Likely the 'Silence Amphitheatre' listed as a stop on locally guided full-day loops.

OSM campsite node tagged name:en='Ranger Station' on the Pantishara-Eldari road near Bugha Moedani, in the southern border strip. Distinct from the central ranger station; a guidepost sits at 41.131529/46.545978. Being in the border zone, camping here is subject to the border-permit rules and wild camping is prohibited.

sites.name_en: Rangers post on the Black Mountain - Kvemo Kedi track
sites.description: OSM-signed rangers post on the 'Black mountain-Kvemo Kedi' track in the park's north-east, the access corridor to Shavi Mta used on day 2 of official routes 5 and 7. A shelter (41.263011/46.628429), toilets (41.263239/46.628525), viewpoint (41.262521/46.628394) and a signed parking-and-picnic area (41.264487/46.634661) cluster just south of it.

sites.name_en: Footpath to the cross (Shavi Mta convent approach)
sites.description: Signed walking trail leaving the Black Mountain track toward a hilltop cross, beside the parking and picnic area. The official route 5/7 hiking leg (3-4 km) runs along this ridge toward the 4th-5th century Shavi Mta convent ruins, with the Alazani valley and Mingachevir reservoir on the right.

Signed viewpoint over the Alazani where the river forms the Georgia-Azerbaijan border, on the Mijniskure road just south of the bungalow camp. The southernmost publicly signed point of the park; border-zone permit required and camping on the riverbank strip is strictly prohibited.

The final approach track to Mijniskure crosses its watercourse repeatedly: OSM maps fords explicitly named 'Road to Mijniskure' at 41.127608/46.588891, 41.128253/46.596993, 41.128574/46.591000 and 41.128682/46.592711, plus an unnamed 'Possible road' ford at 41.128457/46.591754 and further fords at 41.111611/46.643792, 41.120615/46.644315, 41.124437/46.648991 and 41.127101/46.650993. Trip reports single out the last ~5 km into Mijniskure as 4x4-only, through a narrow steep-sided canyon.

Dense ford cluster where the Pantishara-Eldari track runs along the southern floodplain: OSM fords at 41.088339/46.501040, 41.104313/46.492529, 41.105604/46.492107, 41.106948/46.493874, 41.109716/46.497804, 41.111220/46.500136, 41.112186/46.502516, 41.113455/46.503611, 41.116005/46.508303 and 41.126954/46.512868. This is the lowest, wettest and most flood-prone part of the network and lies inside the border zone.

The western track linking Taribana, Chachuna Managed Reserve and the Eldari lowland carries its own ford series — OSM fords at 41.190032/46.239533, 41.198496/46.239554, 41.202343/46.235941, 41.217305/46.224282, 41.271102/46.220405, 41.286599/46.230824 and 41.306587/46.218289. Overlanding guides route Vashlovani-to-David Gareja trips this way, crossing the Iori and continuing to the Iori steppes.

Named OSM track/unclassified road forming the western entry corridor from the town toward Pantishara; segments mapped at 41.344260/46.297399, 41.295063/46.303392, 41.269012/46.326653 and 41.254116/46.389832. Guides put roughly 2 hours' driving between Dedoplistsqaro and Pantishara; clay surface that becomes impassable after rain.

Named route linking the Kasristskali entrance area to the Pantishara canyon and the Alesilebi badlands, ending at the signed end-of-car-way nodes. Segments at 41.238435/46.407392 and a ford at 41.225934/46.366101. Published trail descriptions give about 13 km from Kasristskali to Pantishara valley and Bear Canyon, the first ~9 km undulating before the canyon descent.

Named road (tertiary in its northern part) running from the Karistskali/Kasristskali area south to Mijniskure and passing the Central Bungalows. Segments at 41.286576/46.471812 and 41.232593/46.524946; fords along it at 41.210496/46.541160, 41.225585/46.533700 and 41.262225/46.524005.

Named road running west-east along the southern border strip from Pantishara toward the Eldari lowland, serving Bugha Moedani and the southern ranger station. Segments at 41.130251/46.449272 and 41.115648/46.462601; a ford at 41.149264/46.420496. Inside the border zone, so the permit and no-camping rules apply.

Connector track between the Pantishara arm and the central Vashlovani/ranger-station area, letting the one-day loop be closed without backtracking. Guidepost at 41.223402/46.406081 and viewpoint at 41.223414/46.406088.

Named road/track/path chain climbing from Takhistskali east toward Shavi Mta (Black Mountain): unclassified at 41.188036/46.600563, track at 41.170380/46.654420 and a foot path at 41.172251/46.652244 — i.e. the vehicle track converts to a footpath before the summit ridge. Official route 5 names Imedi Gorge as the approach to the Shavi Mta forest.

sites.name_en: Kaklis Kure (Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument)
sites.description: Peninsula-shaped bight in the Alazani riverbed, 204 ha, entered through a neck only 30-40 m wide; the only place along the Alazani where extensive natural walnut and oak floodplain forest survives. Official route 4: Visitor Centre to Kaklis Kure 60 km one way, 120 km roundtrip, 1 day, off-road vehicle, with a picnic area at the monument. Border-zone registration required.

Actively erupting mud, oil and gas craters (largest 3.5-4 m across) on a plain at 620 m south of the Dali reservoir; 9.7 ha natural monument with a 0.5 km pedestrian path. Official route 3: Visitor Centre to Dali Mountain Reservoir 35 km, 110 km roundtrip, 1 day, off-road vehicle. IMPORTANT: two independent sources agree on this coordinate (Wikipedia 41.245683/45.843617, Georgian Travel Guide 41.24601/45.84399) and it falls far WEST of the stated park bounding box — the monument is a detached unit of Vashlovani Protected Areas, roughly 35 km west of the national park proper, not inside it. Marked low confidence per the bbox sanity rule, though the coordinate itself is well corroborated. Reached only after the border-police checkpoint; guides quote 51 km from Dedoplistsqaro.

sites.name_en: Mount Takhti Tepa (763 m triangulation viewpoint)
sites.description: OSM viewpoint node labelled as Mt Takhti Tepa, 763 m, about 5 km south-east of the mud-volcano monument. Coordinate is far west of the park bounding box, so flagged low per the sanity rule; it appears to be a genuine separate summit label in the Iori/Eldari uplands rather than the mud volcano site itself.

Listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 6380), dated 5th-17th c., on the eastern edge of the Gombori range on the historic road linking the Alazani and Iori plains, in Artsivis Kheoba (Eagle Gorge) Natural Monument ~3-4 km north of Dedoplistsqaro. Built of dressed limestone blocks and Georgian brick across two rock massifs separated by a rock gate, 800-1000 m long: citadel of three terraces on the western massif reached by one narrow path with rock-cut steps, a small defensive building on the eastern massif, and a lower walled refuge ('sakhizno') formed by two parallel walls closing the field between them, whose horizontal masonry is attributed to Vakhtang Gorgasali's time; the main cart-gate was defended by a rectangular tower and a watchtower on the northern crest controlled the Alazani plain. Tradition links it to Queen Tamar; the township was destroyed around 1264-1265 by Berke Khan and survivors relocated to Sighnaghi. COORDINATE NOTE: lon 46.136 lies west of the 46.2-46.8 sanity window - this is correct, the site is ~35 km NW of the park core but is administratively part of Vashlovani Protected Areas via Artsivis Kheoba. Wikipedia/Wikidata give 41.48646/46.13683; OSM 41.48606/46.13578.

Signed interpretation point at a salt (brackish) watercourse on the southern track network — note it is NOT potable, consistent with all guides insisting Mijniskure holds the park's only reliable drinking water. Fords cluster immediately around it at 41.132019/46.575007, 41.138759/46.580182 and 41.144890/46.579170.

Open steppe where the reintroduced goitered gazelle herd (up to ~150 animals) is watched from the track. Official route 8 crosses it; leaving the route or approaching the animals is prohibited, and secondary roads here are reported closed in April-May for the breeding season. Shepherds' huts line the route from October to May.

OSM campsite explicitly named for wind shelter, on the main northern access track about 4 km north of the central ranger station, with a guidepost at 41.250047/46.432526. A further campsite is mapped at 41.323438/46.436057 nearer the park's northern edge.

OSM guest_house on the park's northern fringe — a rare bed option between Dedoplistsqaro and the park interior, relevant because official routes 5-8 are 2-day itineraries and in-park bungalows are limited and need advance booking.

Last village on the northern approach and the namesake of three of the park's named tracks (Kasristskali-Vashlovani, Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi, Karistskali-Mijniskure). Drinking-water points are mapped just south of it at 41.287486/46.463533 and 41.289589/46.458276, and springs at 41.287890/46.466517 and 41.271815/46.441560 — the last water before the interior.

At 845 m the highest named summit found inside the park area in OSM, in the Shavi Mta / Black Mountain block in the north-east, close to the park's published 858 m maximum elevation. Sits above the rangers post on the Black Mountain-Kvemo Kedi track.

sites.name_en: Nearest fuel stations north of the park (Kvemo Kedi / Shiraki area)
sites.description: OSM maps no fuel inside the park; the closest pumps on the northern approach are at 41.372436/46.506565, 41.403563/46.446018, 41.421602/46.380278 and 41.425250/46.383434. Every guide insists on filling up in Dedoplistsqaro (the only full resupply: bazaar, supermarkets, bakeries, tyre shops) because off-road use roughly doubles consumption, and petrol vehicles should carry a jerrycan. No fuel, ATMs or shops beyond the town.

Visitor Centre to the Eagle Gorge entrance is 2.5 km; 7 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium difficulty, car tour integrated with 2-3 km of hiking. Main attractions Khornabuji Fortress, St Elias church and vulture watching. The only Vashlovani route that does not need a 4x4 or a border permit. APA's own trail page instead quotes 7-8 km and 'average' difficulty with a GPX download.

Visitor Centre to Pantishara Gorge 55 km; 130 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium, bicycle or off-road car integrated with 3-4 km hiking. Attractions: city of swallows, Alesilebi badlands, fossils, Vashlovani pistachio 'cavernous' and the ranger station with its 500-900 year old pistachio grove. The coordinate given is the published second waypoint (the central ranger station). Georgian Travel Guide quotes 120 km and 'easy'.

Visitor Centre to Dali Mountain Reservoir 35 km; 110 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium, off-road vehicle only. Heads south-west from Dedoplistsqaro past the Dali reservoir to the mud volcanoes — i.e. away from the national park proper. nationalparks.ge lists the same route as 110 km, 1 day, medium. Guides quote 51 km one way from town and note the site lies beyond the border-police checkpoint, so ID and registration are needed.

sites.name_en: Official route 4: Kaklis Kure - Alazani Floodplain
sites.description: Visitor Centre to Kaklis Kure 60 km; 120 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium, off-road vehicle. Runs south-east through several villages to the Alazani floodplain natural monument, where there is a picnic area. Border-zone registration required (Kaklis Kure is named as one of the three permit-controlled destinations).

sites.name_en: Official route 5: Mijniskure - Shavi Mta (Black Mountain)
sites.description: Visitor Centre to the park's central entrance 50 km; 225 km roundtrip, 2 days, DIFFICULT, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking — the park's hardest official itinerary. Day 1 crosses the park via the Usakhelo viewpoint and descends to Mijniskure for bungalows/tents and fly fishing; day 2 returns to the central entrance, follows Imedi Gorge to the Shavi Mta pheasant forest and picnic area, then hikes the ridge to the 4th-5th century Shavi Mta convent ruins (legend: Queen Ketevan's last night in Kakheti). Georgian Travel Guide gives 220 km with waypoints 41.462242/46.103804, 41.111092/46.646635 and 41.215722/46.43341.

Visitor Centre to the central entrance 50 km; 160 km roundtrip, 2 days, difficult, bicycle or off-road car. Passes the Usakhelo viewpoint and descends to Mijniskure to overnight in riverbank bungalows or tents, with designated fly fishing on the Alazani (about 20 fish species; best in spring and autumn). Listed by APA as 'Midjnisyure Sportuli - Tevzaoba'.

sites.name_en: Official route 7: Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta (Black Mountain)
sites.description: Visitor Centre to Pantishara Gorge 50 km; 200 km roundtrip, 2 days, moderate, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking. Day 1 Pantishara gorge and badlands, then the pistachio/juniper viewpoint, overnighting in the Central Bungalows or tents; day 2 to the central entrance, along Imedi Gorge to the Shavi Mta forest picnic area and on foot to the convent ruins. APA lists a variant as 'Qurcikebis Volier - Shavi Mta' (gazelle enclosure to Black Mountain).

sites.name_en: Official route 8: Land of the Hidden Water
sites.description: Visitor Centre to Pantishara Gorge 50 km; 190 km roundtrip, 2 days, difficult, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking — the route that 'covers almost the whole territory of the National Park'. Day 1: Pantishara gorge geology, then south-east across Samukhi Valley (gazelles; do not leave the route) and down to Mijniskure. Day 2: out through Chighoelta Khevi to the park ranger station, past the Vashlovani cavernous viewpoint and back to Dedoplistsqaro. Shepherds' huts line it October-May.

Soviet-era abandoned airfield on the Shiraki plain, used as the first stop on locally guided full-day Vashlovani loops before the ranger station. Included here as a named route waypoint; I did not fetch a source publishing its coordinate.

sites.name_en: Dali Mountain reservoir and hunting farm
sites.description: Reservoir 35 km south-west of the Visitor Centre, the waypoint on the Takhti-Tepa route; nationalparks.ge also mentions 'the Dali mountain hunting farm, located 45 km from Dedoplistskaro' as an accommodation option. Nominatim returned no node for 'Dali reservoir'/'დალის მთა', so no coordinate is asserted.

sites.name_en: Savanna Guest House and Teo's Cottages, Dedoplistsqaro
sites.description: The two named town bed options used by park visitors: Savanna Guest House (family-run, meals and a shop, lunchboxes with 24h notice) and Teo's Cottages (walking distance from Eagle Canyon). Relevant because park routes start early and in-park bungalows need advance booking. No published coordinates found.

The park's in-field accommodation hub, tagged tourism=hostel + landuse=commercial (OSM way/1322451821); the official map calls it the 'central bungalows'. Reached via the central entrance of the national park, 50 km from the Dedoplistsqaro administration. Coordinate is the OSM polygon centroid.

Ranger office building (OSM way/474150182, building=office, name 'rangerpost') immediately adjacent to the central bungalows. The official map's route 2 notes a trail from the park ranger station to the grove of ancient pistachio trees.

Riverside base on the Alazani floodplain at the park's far south-east corner (OSM node/1182746361, tourism=hostel), with a separate information point (node/4424085391), an attraction node and a water well at 41.1110, 46.6467. Official routes 5 and 6 overnight here; fly fishing is permitted.
OSM node/9804175417, name:en 'Ranger Station', tagged tourism=camp_site — a staffed post that also serves as a camping spot, 40 m from the Bugha Moedani viewpoint. Start of official route 7.

Rangers post (OSM node/4424146593) in the park's eastern Shavi Mta / Zilcha sector, with a shelter, bench, toilets and viewpoint clustered 1 km south around 41.2625-41.2632, 46.6274-46.6285. Gateway to the Shavi Mta convent trail.

Official administration and visitor centre with exhibition hall, at Baratashvili St 5, Dedoplistsqaro — outside the park, 130 km / 2 h from Tbilisi. Check-in here is mandatory before entering the national park. Excavated Southern elephant bones from the Datviskhevi trail are kept in this building. No coordinate is published, only the street address.

Highest summit of the national park at 845 m (OSM node/8062013696 ele=845; Wikidata Q12864765 gives 846 m at 41.2658, 46.6364; GeoNames 610841 'Mta Zilcha K'osmat'k'a' gives 854 m; PeakVisor 847 m with 217 m prominence). Russian Soviet-map form is Gora Zil'cha-Kosmatka. Crown of the Shavi Mta massif.

428 m hill (OSM node/8061747863, natural=peak) whose name means 'nameless mountain'. Named on official routes 5 and 6 as the Usakhelo viewpoint over the badlands, passed on the descent from the central park entrance to Mijniskure.
578 m mountain in the park's north-west, Wikidata Q12870536 (Georgian label only, no English). Lends its name to the Kumuro sector; the Kumra stream (კუმრა) drains east of it.

Mountain group (Russian 'gory' = mountains), 747 m, GeoNames 799095 / Wikidata Q24686784 — an unlabelled Wikidata item whose name had to be recovered from its GeoNames P1566 link. Soviet-topographic toponym.

Named ridge (Russian 'khrebet' = range) on the park's northern edge below the Shiraki plain, dem 643 m. GeoNames 799099 / Wikidata Q24686780 (mountain range, no label — name recovered via the GeoNames id). Classic Soviet-sheet label.

Viewpoint (OSM node/11891968791, 'Alesilebi view') over the eroded clay pillars and columns the official map calls 'razor-sharp badlands' that 'at first sight look like man-made castles'. PeakVisor describes the Alesilebi (Pointed Rocks) as clay cliffs 59-70 m high with ridges named Pantishira and Datviskhevi. An OSM track is named Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi.

OSM node/10836240203 (natural=tree, name 'Old Pistachio') beside a 'Flora' interpretive board at the same location. The official map states the grove near the ranger station holds pistachios mostly over 500 years old with the oldest over 900 years — described as the oldest pistachio tree in Europe.
Viewpoint (OSM node/11553249495) in the central park sector between Kumuro and the visitor centre, above the cliff belt mapped at 41.195-41.218, 46.49-46.50.
Named gorge with an interpretive information point (OSM node/4424146495) on the Mijniskure road in the park's south-east. Name means 'gorge of the shales/slates'.
Ravine (Russian 'ovrag'), dem 459 m, GeoNames 799094 / Wikidata Q24686785 — an unlabelled Wikidata item resolved through its GeoNames link. Soviet-sheet toponym; 'darasi' is Turkic for valley.
Ravine at the foot of the Patara Shiraki plain (Georgian 'bolo' = end), dem 617 m. GeoNames 799092 / Wikidata Q24686786 (no label, no type — recovered via GeoNames). Soviet-sheet toponym.

Gorge named on the official trekking map as the corridor from the central park entrance to the Shavi Mta forest on routes 5 and 7. PeakVisor renders it 'Imeda Valley'. No coordinate in any source fetched and nothing under this name in OSM or Nominatim — genuinely missing from structured geodata.

Per Georgian Wikipedia, the connecting gorge between the Patara Shiraki and Eldari plains that forms the national park's western boundary. No coordinate published; not present in OSM or GeoNames. Useful as a boundary-defining feature if it can later be digitised.

Ruined settlement inside the national park (OSM node/8927317168, historic=ruins + ruins=village). Registered as a Georgian cultural property, Wikidata Q42771692, which carries the Georgian name but NO coordinate — this OSM node is the only georeference found, making it a valuable cross-reference. One of very few archaeological sites mapped within the park itself.

sites.name_en: Shavi Mta Convent ruins (cross on the monastery site)
sites.description: OSM node/4424146895 (amenity=place_of_worship, 'cross on the former monastery site') at the 4th-5th c. church ruins on Shavi Mta, 130 m below Zilcha summit; only floor and foundation fragments survive. Legend holds that Queen Ketevan the Martyr of Kakheti spent her last night here before leaving for Persia. Reached by the marked footpath to the cross from 41.2649, 46.6352.

Per Georgian Wikipedia this river marks the national park's southern boundary. The only georeference found is the OSM interpretive node 'ლეკის (მლაშე) წყალი' (node/4424146494), which pairs the name with Mlashetskali (salt water) — so the two names appear to refer to the same saline system. Coordinate is that interpretive point, not a channel centroid.
man_made=water_well (OSM node/4681597570) at the Mijniskure visitor centre, 40 m from the hostel node — the only mapped well in the park's southern floodplain camp.

Unnamed natural=spring (OSM node/13270249903) in the park's northern sector on the Kasristskali-Vashlovani corridor. Water sources are scarce in this semi-desert, so unnamed springs are operationally significant.
Unnamed natural=spring (OSM node/13765782946) on the northern park margin below Kvemo Kedi, on the Black mountain-Kvemo Kedi track. Unnamed in OSM; no gazetteer entry.
OSM node/13294854338, tourism=camp_site, name 'Wind protected' — a named-for-function pitch in the park's central sector between Kasristskali and the pistachio grove.
Campsite (OSM node/1182749665) with an adjoining picnic site (node/11645362504, 41.2155, 46.4325) and viewpoint (node/12116556682) in the central Kumuro sector, close to the ancient pistachio grove.
Unnamed tourism=camp_site (OSM node/13294837727) on the park's northern boundary below the Shiraki plain. No name in any gazetteer.

Guest house (OSM node/11833332872, tourism=guest_house) at Dilicha on the park's northern edge — the only private accommodation mapped inside the protected-area corridor, as against the state bungalows at the visitor centres.

Grassland steppe plain forming the park's northern boundary, Wikidata Q4524215 (ru: Ширакская степь). GeoNames 611979 'Shirakis Vake' records it as V.GRSLD grassland at 41.35, 46.45, dem 592 m, with alternates Shiraki Steppe, Schiraker Steppe, Shirakskaya Step', Sirak Colu. Visible from the St Elias church on the Eagle Gorge route; a 'Shiraki view' viewpoint sits at 41.3235, 46.3073.

Named tract in the park's centre, dem 533 m; GeoNames 799093, classed L.AREA. 'Urochishche' is the Soviet-map generic for a named natural locality with no other classification — a pure Soviet-sheet survival with no Wikidata or OSM counterpart.

Village on the park's northern edge (Wikidata Q16374146; GeoNames 612451, Russian alternate Malyye Shiraki = 'Lesser Shiraki', dem 592 m). Three OSM farmland polygons carry the name across 41.266-41.290, 46.360-46.372, and the Ovrag Patara-Shirakis-Bolo ravine marks the plain's edge.

Village forming the park's northern boundary with its agricultural plots, per Georgian Wikipedia. GeoNames 614925, dem 557 m, Russian alternate Bol'shiye Shiraki ('Greater Shiraki'). Nominatim returns an OSM hamlet of the same name 8 km east at 41.4172, 46.4212, so the two sources disagree on placement.

Village at 500 m on the park's northern approach and the main road junction into it (Wikidata Q12865640; GeoNames 614102, whose alternate names include El'dar, El'darskiy and Eldari — the Soviet-era name). Has a public school (41.2879, 46.4634), town hall (41.2876, 46.4646) and ambulance station (41.2872, 46.4666). Four OSM tracks radiate from it.

Village at 700 m on the park's northern boundary, Wikidata Q4218649 (ru: Квемо-Кеди); GeoNames 613466 places it at 41.37110, 46.51061, dem 728 m, alternates Kedi-Kvemo, Tsiteli. Terminus of the Tsnori-Dedoplistsqaro-Kvemo Kedi road (ref შ 39) and of the Black mountain-Kvemo Kedi track.

Village at 210 m in the park's north-east near the Alazani, Wikidata Q4403448; GeoNames 611454 at 41.32287, 46.66725, dem 235 m, alternates Tsiteli-Sabatlo / Siteli-Sabatlo. Has an ambulance station, school, place of worship and drinking-water point. Start of the Sabatlo-Black Mountain track.

Village at 280 m on the park's northern margin, Wikidata Q12869935; GeoNames 12109822 at 41.37397, 46.56942, dem 273 m. Named for the painter Niko Pirosmani. apa.gov.ge locates the Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument 'to the southwest from Village Pirosmani', making it the reference settlement for that monument. Has a public school at 41.3750, 46.5652.

Populated place recorded in GeoNames 614688, dem 621 m, inside the park's northern sector. Coordinates are rounded to whole minutes, the signature of a Soviet-sheet transcription, and no Wikidata, OSM or Nominatim entry exists — so it is very likely a depopulated or renamed settlement rather than a live one. Flagged for ground-truthing against satellite imagery.

Named locality (OSM node/760262846, place=locality; ru: Мижднис Куре) at the park's southern tip on the Alazani floodplain, giving its name to the visitor centre, the bungalow camp and two official routes. Name means roughly 'boundary bay'. PeakVisor renders it 'Midhnis Kure basin' with an 8 km descent.

Unpopulated named locality ('Pshav's cove') on the Alazani beside Mijniskure. The toponym records the Pshav highlanders who, alongside the Tush, worked the Shiraki/Vashlovani winter pastures as hired shepherds; the same settler community is documented building a shrine on the Khatis Gora mound further north. Mapped in OSM only; not in the heritage registry.

Named locality (OSM node/8062072322, place=locality) on the park's eastern flank toward the Alazani border. Turkic-derived toponym, part of a cluster of 'kutkhe' (corner) localities in this sector: Kadros Kutkhe 41.3058/46.6990, Kuraghanis Kutkhe 41.3245/46.6948, Almalis Kutkhe 41.2879/46.7244.

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument (Kaklis Kure)
sites.description: Natural monument of Vashlovani Protected Areas, established 2003: 204.4 ha of liana-draped natural floodplain forest in a peninsula-shaped bight of the Alazani right bank at 165 m, rich in perennial walnut, ash, oak and elm — the only surviving extensive habitat of common walnut and common oak in Georgia. Name means 'Bight of the Walnut Trees'. Coordinate converted from the official apa.gov.ge UTM 38N value X 638346 Y 4580257; the OSM locality node sits 430 m away at 41.3657, 46.6553. Entry point 30-40 m wide; 1 km pedestrian route, 56 km / 1 h 30 from Dedoplistsqaro.

sites.name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forest interpretive site, Mijniskure
sites.description: tourism=information board titled 'Floodplain Forest' (OSM node/10836240492) at the Mijniskure camp, and a paired 'Semi-Desert' board at 41.1323, 46.5304 — the park's interpretive pairing of its two signature habitats. Distinct from the Kaklis Kure natural monument 28 km north.

Abandoned Soviet airbase on the Shiraki plain at the park's northern boundary, 547 m (Wikidata Q6047327; GeoNames 799103 classes it S.AIRQ abandoned airfield at 41.37953, 46.36739, elev 549 m, alternate name Zemo Kedi). A large, unmistakable feature for satellite-imagery cross-checking and a useful control point.

Natural monument of Vashlovani Protected Areas, 1.74 km2, protected since 1935, IUCN III. A two-part site: a limestone canyon plus adjacent forest holding the 5th c. Khornabuji fortress. Over 60-80 bird species including nesting black stork, griffon and the rare Egyptian vulture; sole Georgian locality of the endemic Campanula kachetica and of rare oriental thuja. Coordinate converted from the official apa.gov.ge UTM 38N X 591747 Y 4593825, landing 62 m from the OSM 'Eagle Ravine' viewpoint (node/4424086003) — the mapped natural=gorge way/1381273992 centres at 41.4929, 46.0978. Access 4 km north of Dedoplistsqaro, 2 km paved then 2 km gravel forest road. CONFIDENCE REDUCED ONLY BY GEOMETRY: lat 41.49 / lon 46.10 falls outside the stated sanity window, because this monument is a detached unit of the complex well north-west of the national park itself, not an error.

Limestone hill on the Eagle Gorge route (OSM node/13727363043, natural=peak) with a viewpoint 40 m west; the 5th-7th c. Church of St Elias Tezbiteli, restored 2008, stands at 41.4417, 46.1090 about 45 m above the rock base, reached by a stair and footpath. Kochebi Lake, the Shiraki plain, the Taribana valley and the Kotsakhura ridge are all named as visible from it. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window, 3 km from Dedoplistsqaro.

Natural monument of Vashlovani Protected Areas, established 2003. Actively erupting mud craters and vents discharging mud, oil and gas from sandstones and clays, the largest crater 3.5-4 m across; 9.7 ha total (apa.gov.ge also says the craters themselves occupy 1 ha), 620 m elevation, 0.5 km / 30 min pedestrian path. Lies south of the Dali water reservoir on the Iori, parallel to the Takhti-Tepha range; 37 km from Dedoplistsqaro, the last 15 km unpaved. Coordinate converted from the official apa.gov.ge UTM 38N X 570695 Y 4566331, landing 45 m from the English Wikipedia value 41.245683, 45.843617 — two independent sources agreeing. FAILS THE SANITY WINDOW on longitude by ~0.43 deg and sits ~35 km west of the park's west edge: this is correct, not an error, because the monument is a detached unit of the protected-areas complex. PeakVisor reports roughly two dozen active volcanoes in the wider zone.

Mud volcano at 450 m, Wikidata Q130746546 (typed both mud volcano and mountain; Georgian label only). PeakVisor treats Kilakupra as a mud-volcano zone alongside Takhti-Tepa. LOW CONFIDENCE ON LOCATION RELATIVE TO THE PARK: lon 45.77 is ~0.5 deg outside the sanity window and about 45 km west of the park, in the Chachuna/Dali sector rather than Vashlovani National Park proper.

412 m mountain (GeoNames 799693, dem 386 m), the 'Dali Mountain' named as the main waypoint of official route 3 from Dedoplistsqaro to the Takhti-Tepa mud volcanoes. LOW CONFIDENCE ON PROXIMITY: lon 45.87 is well outside the sanity window, ~35 km west of the park, though it is squarely on the official Vashlovani route network.

Reservoir on the Iori, Wikidata Q16368012 (ru: Водохранилище Дали); the official route 3 waypoint, 35 km from the visitor centre, with the Takhti-Tepa monument immediately south of it and the access road crossing the dam. LOW CONFIDENCE ON PROXIMITY: lon 45.88 is outside the sanity window and ~34 km west of the park.

Steppe plain, GeoNames 866049 (T.PLN), dem 437 m. This is the 'Taribana valley' named on the official Eagle Gorge route as visible south from the St Elias church, and the Taribana-Chachuna-Eldari track is named for it. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window on longitude, west of Dedoplistsqaro.

Named ridge, GeoNames 799096 (T.MTS), dem 460 m. Matches the 'Kotsakhura ridge' / 'Kotsakhura Mountain Range' named on the official Eagle Gorge route as the southern skyline from the St Elias church — an instance where a travel description and the Soviet-sheet gazetteer can be tied together. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window on longitude.

Ravine, GeoNames 799097, dem 376 m, on the western approach between Dedoplistsqaro and the park. Coordinates rounded to whole minutes — a Soviet-sheet transcription. Marginally outside the sanity window on longitude.

sites.name_en: Georgian Border Police checkpoint, southern park boundary
sites.description: Border police post (OSM way/998796932, amenity=police + building=yes, name:en 'border checkpoint') on the Pantishara-Eldari track at the park's southern frontier with Azerbaijan, near the Iori. The Georgia-Azerbaijan international boundary way/283675601 runs through 41.1229, 46.4482. Visitors are required to carry ID in the park for this reason.
amenity=police + building=yes named 'border checkpoint' (OSM way/998800894) on the park's southern edge between Bugha Moedani and Mijniskure. Coordinate is the OSM polygon centroid.

sites.name_en: Border police post, western park boundary
sites.description: Border police building (OSM way/1105224457, name:en 'border police checkpoint') on the park's western edge above the Iori, adjacent to a landuse=military parcel at 41.1697, 46.2965. Coordinate is the OSM polygon centroid.

sites.name_en: Border police post, eastern park boundary
sites.description: Border police building (OSM way/1105206643, name:en 'border police checkpoint') in the park's eastern Shavi Mta sector near the Alazani frontier, on the Takhis tskali-Shavi mta track. Coordinate is the OSM polygon centroid.

Unclassified track linking Kasristskali village to Pantishara Gorge and the Alesilebi badlands (OSM way/48844795). Nominatim also returns a waterway of this name at 41.2308, 46.3619, i.e. the track follows the Pantishara streambed. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Dirt road descending to the Mijniskure camp on the Alazani (OSM way/1432246847, surface=dirt); a footway continuation carries the same name at 41.1116, 46.6463, and Nominatim also returns a watercourse of this name at 41.1263, 46.6280 — the road follows the drainage. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Dirt road from the Mijniskure floodplain camp up to Takhistskali (OSM way/495066508; path continuation at 41.1293, 46.6528). First leg of the climb from the Alazani to the Shavi Mta sector. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Dirt road from Takhistskali to the Shavi Mta massif (OSM way/1349195377; path continuation at 41.1731, 46.6530). Nominatim returns it for the Georgian query 'შავი მთა', i.e. it is the principal named access to Black Mountain. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Dirt road traversing the park north to south from Kasristskali to Mijniskure (OSM way/102156443; further segments at 41.2866/46.4718 and 41.2326/46.5249). Note the OSM name transliterates the village as 'karistsqali' rather than 'kasristsqali'. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.
Unpaved road into the Shavi Mta sector (OSM way/256957960); an 'Ols abandoned road' path parallels it at 41.2286, 46.5557. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.
Unpaved road connecting the Shavi Mta sector to Kvemo Kedi on the park's northern boundary (OSM way/102156399). Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.
Unpaved road from Sabatlo village into the Shavi Mta / Zilcha sector (OSM way/266103477), the eastern approach to the rangers post and convent ruins. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Track from the central Vashlovani sector to Mijniskure (OSM way/48845846, highway=track). Note Nominatim mis-assigns this way to Akhmeta Municipality though it lies in Dedoplistsqaro. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

Unpaved road from Kasristskali into the central Vashlovani sector (OSM way/48845978), serving the pistachio grove and the Kumuro campsite. A 'Pantishara-Vashlovani' track (way/256957965) branches at 41.2259, 46.4166. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

The only classified road serving the park's northern boundary, OSM way/164314206, highway=tertiary, ref შ 39 — the paved trunk approach from Tsnori via Dedoplistsqaro. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

OSM way/723115023 is a tertiary unpaved road whose NAME is literally 'Damaged main road. Avoid it', with way/60118565 'Damaged main road bypass' as the alternative at 41.3257, 46.3966. Included because any routing layer built from OSM will otherwise route traffic onto it. Coordinate is an OSM way centroid.

sites.name_en: Datviskhevi trailhead (end of the vehicle road)
sites.description: Interpretive node marking the end of the drivable road (OSM node/4424085098, name:en 'end of car way'), where the Pantishara - Datvis Khevi (Bear Gorge) walking trail begins; a second node of the same name is at 41.2428, 46.3695 and a trail map board at 41.2373, 46.3655. Official route 2 is a car tour integrated with 3-4 km of hiking.

sites.name_en: Footpath to the cross (Shavi Mta convent trail)
sites.description: Marked footpath (OSM node/4424146592) from the parking and picnic area at 41.2645, 46.6347 up the ridge slope to the Shavi Mta convent ruins and cross, with broadleaf forest on one side and views over the Alazani valley and Mingachevir Reservoir on the other.

Breeding enclosure for goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa), the park's flagship species, extinct locally in the 1960s and reintroduced from 2013 with about 150 animals now present. Its existence is confirmed by apa.gov.ge listing official trail 7 as 'ქურციკების ვოლიერი - შავი მთა' (gazelle enclosure - Black Mountain), and the Bugha Moedani ranger station at 41.1256, 46.5386 is the start of that route. NO SOURCE FETCHED GIVES A COORDINATE and the name returns nothing in OSM, Nominatim, Wikidata or GeoNames — reported without lat/lon rather than guessed from the trail endpoint.

Hillfort recorded in Wikidata (Q16417651) as a 'habitation in Qakh, Azerbaijan' with sitelinks in four Wikipedia editions. It falls inside the Vashlovani bounding box but lies across the Alazani on the Azerbaijani side of the border, ~2 km east of the park's eastern limit. No excavation or dating information was found.

historic=archaeological_site in OSM (way/1049119217) whose description tag reads 'Alban Kilsəsi Burunqovaq' — a Caucasian Albanian church site immediately south of the park's southern boundary in Azerbaijan. Unnamed in the name field, so easily missed; no Wikidata or GeoNames entry. Coordinate is the OSM polygon centroid.

Azerbaijani village directly on the park's southern boundary (OSM node/3423586346; Wikidata Q4908076 at 41.093421, 46.441869), with a school, cemetery and a landuse=military parcel at 41.0992, 46.4418. The nearest settlement to the park's southern frontier and a useful reference for the Iori crossing.

Azerbaijani hamlet (Wikidata Q4848029; OSM node/2844519875 at 41.1979, 46.7246) just east of the park boundary in Qakh district, with its own named access road (Üzümlükənd yolu, ref Y34-05). Inside the sanity window, outside the park.

Azerbaijani protected area, Wikidata Q12844337 (typed national park, no English-language description), facing the Vashlovani complex across the Alazani to the south-east. Inside the sanity window but outside the park bbox; relevant as the transboundary counterpart of the Vashlovani reserve.

Azerbaijani protected wilderness area, Wikidata Q4186734, immediately south-west of the park across the Iori and named for the same Eldar/Eldari landscape unit as the park's southern lowland — it protects the Eldar pine. Marginally outside the sanity window on longitude.

Mountain in Azerbaijan named for the Iori river, Wikidata Q21980828 (which carries two near-identical duplicate P625 statements, 41.150555 and 41.15056 — a sign of hand-entered data). Just west of the park's south-western corner, marginally outside the sanity window on longitude.

Lake at 618 m, Wikidata Q24687079 / GeoNames 866040 'Ozero Patara-Tba' (dem 617 m); OSM relation/7096124 centres at 41.4623, 46.1761. North of Dedoplistsqaro near the Artsivi Gorge monument. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window; included because it is one of the few named standing waters in the municipality and serves as a control point.

Municipal seat at 800 m, Wikidata Q1010979, GeoNames 7667712; the park's gateway town, 130 km / 2 h from Tbilisi, holding the Vashlovani Protected Areas administration and visitor centre (Baratashvili St 5), the regional archive (Q81165839 at 41.301268, 46.206216) and the museum of peoples' friendship. All eight official park routes start here. Outside the park bbox and the sanity window, north-west of the park as stated in the brief.

Second-order administrative division containing the entire Vashlovani Protected Areas complex, Wikidata Q1490703 (NOT Q1132123, which is in Japan — a trap for anyone querying P131), GeoNames 611448, OSM relation/2027334 with centroid 41.3169, 46.2430. Querying P131=Q1490703 returns 70 items, mostly cultural properties with no coordinates, which is the main reason so many church and archaeological records in this municipality remain ungeoreferenced.

sites.name_en: Khoranta ancient city site (Khorantha / city of Hereti)
sites.description: Medieval town site on the Eldari plain at the western foot of the Samukhi ridge, inside Vashlovani NP; listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 15581, dated 5th c. BC - 9th c. AD). Georgian sources identify it with the city of Hereti founded by the legendary Heros, capital of the Kingdom of Hereti, which ceased to exist after Berke Khan's campaign of 1265. Excavated 1965 by L. Chilashvili (who localised the city, ~10 ha in several quarters separated by dry gullies) and re-trenched in 2009 by Ilia State University at the foot of the Alesilebi ridge; two cultural layers (pre-Christian and early Christian), qvevri and tile fragments some bearing crosses, and a stone building interpreted as a church.

Archaeological iron-smelting workshop inside Vashlovani NP, ~2.5 km NW of the Khoranta town site (heritage registry id 24280). The registry records large slag fragments clearly visible around the workshop; physical state 'very bad'. Unlisted object (no protection status).

Mound settlement (gora-namosakhlari) on a high hill at Mijniskure on the Alazani, at the extreme SE tip of the park; heritage registry id 23220, dated to the second half of the 1st millennium, physical state 'very bad'. NOTE: OpenStreetMap carries a node with the identical Georgian name tagged iron-age at 41.06184, 46.50305 (~13 km SW, near the Iori); the official registry polygon is the coordinate given here.

sites.name_en: Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) complex - convent ruins
sites.description: Ruined religious complex on the Shavi Mta / Zilcha ridge inside the park (heritage registry id 26771, Kvemo Kedi community). The registry describes rubble-stone wall remains actively incorporating straw-tempered Late Antique bricks, with Late Antique roof-tile fragments scattered over the ruins; tradition holds it was a monastery. APA and nationalparks.ge date the convent to the 4th-5th c., with only the foundation and fragments of the floor surviving, and record the legend that Ketevan the Martyr, Queen of Kakheti, spent her last night in Georgia here before being taken through the Eldari lowland to Persia. OSM maps the spot as 'ჯვარი ნამონასტრალზე' (cross on a former monastery site) at 41.26637, 46.63722.

Remains of an Antique-period pagan temple at the northern edge of the park near Sabatlo village (heritage registry id 26772). Exploratory excavation recorded round stone column bases in situ; physical state 'destroyed'. Unlisted object.

sites.name_en: Palaeolithic open-air station, Kvemo Kedi (park north boundary)
sites.description: Stone Age (Palaeolithic) open-air station at the northern boundary of Vashlovani NP, heritage registry id 24307. Finds recorded: a low broad irregular flint flake with a wide smooth striking platform, and a borer made on an elongated oval flint flake. The oldest dated human trace recorded in the immediate park area.

sites.name_en: Zilcha peak (ridge hosting the Shavi Mta complex)
sites.description: 845 m summit in the eastern part of Vashlovani NP; the Shavi Mta convent ruins sit on its crest. Wikidata Q12864765; OSM node 8062013696 gives ele=845. The adjoining ridge is mapped as Zilchis Seri (Q125305823, 41.27778, 46.63306).
