Park ranger post in the Shavi Mta sector, the access point for the hiking trail to the Shavi Mta convent ruins. Picnic shelter, toilets and an interpretive board are mapped within ~100 m; the marked trailhead ('საფეხმავლო ბილიკი ჯვრისკენ' - footpath to the cross) is at 41.26487, 46.63523.

sites.name_en: Mijniskure - former settlement locality and park outpost
sites.description: Locality (no permanent population) at the extreme SE corner of Georgia where the Alazani crosses into Azerbaijan; the name means roughly 'boundary cove/outpost'. Today a park outpost: visitor/ranger building at 41.11175, 46.64620, seven chalets/bungalows 41.1111-41.1116 / 46.6456-46.6473, water well, toilets and guideposts. A registry-listed settlement mound (id 23220) lies immediately above it.

Ranger/visitor building and bungalow camp on the Alazani floodplain at Mijniskure, the overnight base for routes 5 and 6 on the official APA trekking map. Interpretive board 'Floodplain Forest' and a 'Border Alazani River' viewpoint (41.10778, 46.63978) are adjacent.

The only inhabited village inside the Vashlovani bounding box (population 214 in 2014, elevation ~500 m; Wikidata Q12865640). Its origin in the mid-20th century is tied to the winter pastures used by Kakhetian and historically Tushetian livestock farmers. Public school (41.28791, 46.46343), town hall (41.28756, 46.46457), drinking-water points and a cemetery are mapped. Not the same place as the Kasristskali kurgan group near Dedoplistsqaro town.

Cemetery polygon mapped beside Kasristskali village inside the park (OSM way 102421802, imported from JumpStart International survey data). No name, denomination or date recorded; no heritage-registry entry.

Dispersed transhumant sheep stations across the park interior - the living continuation of the Tusheti-Shiraki transhumance. The official APA map states that from October to May shepherds' huts line the route from Samukhi Valley towards Mijniskure and that from February to April the stations are full of lambs. OSM maps stables at 41.27286/46.51267, 41.26222/46.52120, 41.25761/46.51943, 41.28725/46.48429 and 41.25930/46.37348, a barn at 41.27353/46.69133, and ~66 farmyard polygons within the park bbox. The coordinate given is one representative stable.

Interpretive point marking the Samukhi plain in the south-central park, on APA route 8 ('Land of the hidden water'); the Khoranta town site lies at the western foot of the Samukhi ridge per the heritage registry. The route through Samukhi is where the APA map locates the seasonal shepherds' huts.

The Agency of Protected Areas lists 'Samukhi V century city-fortress remains' among Vashlovani's fortification monuments, but gives no location. No matching record exists in the Georgian national immovable-monuments registry (searched for 'სამუხ'), and no coordinate was found in any source. May be a loose reference to the Khoranta site, which the registry places at the western foot of the Samukhi ridge.

APA lists a 'Pantishara watchtower' among the park's fortification structures; a secondary Georgian tourism source describes old caves in the Pantishara/Alesilebi cliffs that 'used to be watch spots for coming enemy troops'. No coordinate is published and no registry record exists (searched 'პანტიშარ'). The Pantishara canyon itself is at 41.23153, 46.36246.

APA lists a 'Mijnis Bay watchtower' alongside the Pantishara one as a fortification structure of the Vashlovani area. No coordinate published and no separate registry record; the only registered monument at Mijniskure is the settlement mound (id 23220, 41.111374/46.639948), which may be what is meant.

APA's Vashlovani sightseeing page names 'villages Upadara and Kaladara' among the remains of ancient cities and villages in the protected area, with no further detail. A search of the Georgian immovable-monuments registry for 'უფადარ' returns nothing, and no coordinate was found in any source.

Hill named 'Kaladara' inside Vashlovani NP, recorded in Wikidata (Q24684427) as a mountain in Georgia. Offered as a candidate location for the 'village Kaladara' that APA lists among the park's ancient settlement remains, but nothing confirms archaeology here. A distinct, registry-recorded 'Kaladara (Kadirdagh) settlements' group exists ~28 km NW at 41.413047/46.183726.

sites.name_en: Georgian Border Police post, Iori sector
sites.description: Border-guard building mapped at the southern edge of the park near the Iori, tagged police=border_guard with name:en 'border checkpoint'. The whole southern and eastern park perimeter is the Georgia-Azerbaijan state border and was a restricted Soviet border zone; visitors are still required to carry ID inside the park.

Second checkpoint building inside the park, tagged amenity=police / police=checkpoint, on the track between the central bungalows and the Alazani sector. An interpretive board is mapped at the same spot.

428 m summit and named viewpoint on the descent to Mijniskure; the APA trekking map's routes 5 and 6 both pass 'the viewpoint of Usakhelo' before dropping to the Alazani. Not to be confused with the Usakhelo Gora archaeological mound on the Shiraki plain (41.391864/46.351982).

sites.name_en: Fossil southern-elephant bone find site, Datvis Khevi
sites.description: Marked find spot on the Datvis Khevi (Bear Gorge) trail where fossil bones of a southern elephant (Archidiskodon) were recovered; the largest bone is 87 cm long and the excavated material is kept in the Protected Areas administration building in Dedoplistsqaro. Fossilised wood and seashells outcrop between the rock layers along the same trail.

sites.name_en: Pantishara Canyon (City of Swallows / Alesilebi badlands)
sites.description: Narrow gorge with vertical eroded cliffs that look like man-made castles, riddled with swallows' nests (the 'City of Swallows', OSM info node 41.23662/46.36693). Ilia State University's 2009 trench on the Khoranta town site was placed at the foot of the Alesilebi ridge here; an 'Alesilebi view' viewpoint is mapped at 41.22322/46.35264.

Side gorge off Pantishara carrying the park's main marked hiking trail; the fossil-bearing horizons and the southern-elephant bone find lie along it. Trailhead infrastructure (basic hut, camp site, picnic site, toilets and the 'Fossilized World of Vashlovani' board) is clustered at 41.2372-41.2378 / 46.3651-46.3655.

In-park accommodation node (nine bungalows mapped, 41.1595-41.1601 / 46.5659-46.5673) used as the overnight base on the multi-day APA routes. The Protected Areas administration and main visitor centre are outside the park in Dedoplistsqaro town, N5 Baratashvili St.

Village on the park's northern edge, population 391 (2014, Wikidata Q4403448); the administrative settlement for the Sabatlo natadzrali temple site 1.4 km to the NE. An Orthodox place of worship (41.32154, 46.66752), school and cemetery (41.32039, 46.66635) are mapped; a further Muslim cemetery is mapped at 41.35321, 46.67149.

Listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 15570, 4th-14th c.) in the Georgia-Azerbaijan border zone, opposite the Azerbaijani settlement of Kesamani, on the left bank of the Iori on a high rocky ridge; ~1.9 km west of the park's western boundary, in the Chachuna direction. Its historical name is unknown; discovered in the late 2000s and surveyed by Ilia State University in 2009. Spread over several hectares on two terraces with legible streets and rubble walls, a citadel with a 1 m-thick circuit wall and an oval tower on a rectangular pedestal (4.6 m diameter, 3 m of wall standing), and a church (13.3 x 12 m) of local ashlar inside the citadel. The southern part of the site is now in Azerbaijan.

Second listed cultural heritage monument of the Ivrispiri (Iori-bank) group, registry id 15562, ~1.2 km NW of the medieval town site and just west of the park boundary. The registry's polygon layer gives the name, listing status and geometry but the descriptive record was not returned by the service, so date and excavation history are unknown.

Pair of iron-smelting workshops on the Iori plateau west of the park (registry id 22968): one on open ground measuring 50 x 50 m with slag heaps and collapsed hollows, a second on a level platform 30 m across with several visible slag piles. Part of a wide metallurgical landscape - the registry records at least five further iron-workshop clusters in Dedoplistsqaro municipality.

Listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 23014), 12th-10th c. BC, 16 ha, on the ridge just NW of the park boundary. A ~2 ha citadel on a high mountain spur is enclosed by two circuit walls and defensive ditches with zigzag-offset gateways flanked by dry-stone towers; aerial photography shows a single large building inside the upper enclosure interpreted as a temple. One of the two type-sites (with Didnauri) of the Shiraki Plain Late Bronze/Early Iron Age fortified-settlement system studied by the 2024 EGQSJ landscape-archaeology survey. OSM maps it as 'Nazarlebi Early Iron Age Sanctuary and Settlement' at 41.34036/46.24076.

Late Bronze Age settlement cluster and burial ground adjoining the Nazarlebi proto-urban site (registry id 22931). Records a round citadel 80 m across with a double defensive terrace and gateways flanked by square cobble-built towers, a lower town 400 x 300 m with its own rampart, a second settlement 2 km SW levelled by tractor, and two further oval fortified settlements 1 km apart to the east.

National-category listed monument (registry id 11418), Late Bronze/Early Iron Age (12th-9th c. BC), on the western Didi Shiraki plain at km 9 of the Dedoplistsqaro-Kvemo Kedi road, ~7 km north of the park. Discovered in 2014 from satellite imagery by the expedition of Konstantine Pitskhelauri; ~35 ha per satellite mapping (14 ha of core per the 2024 survey). Enclosed by a 1.5 km-long, 7 m-wide clay-and-timber defensive wall, apparently destroyed by an earthquake; excavation revealed ritual buildings, a water supply system and four tombs with early-10th-c. BC ceramics, stone tools and bronzes, one holding an elite warrior buried with his dagger and a non-local arrowhead lodged in his abdomen. Wikipedia gives 41.41472/46.22306; OSM 41.41444/46.22200.

Early Iron Age mound settlement (registry id 23132), 8th-7th c. BC, on the Shiraki plain ~4.5 km north of the park boundary. A circular artificial mound ringed by an earthen defensive rampart; excavation exposed several houses with plastered floors and plastered ovens plus two pits, and yielded clay seals, ceramics, Scythian two-bladed arrowheads, bronze armour fragments and a bronze standard. Named in the 2024 EGQSJ survey as an example of the plain's highly visible mounds.

Multi-layer Early Iron Age mound settlement (registry id 23133), 8th-7th c. BC, on the Shiraki plain north of the park. One layer was destroyed by an invasion at the start of the 7th c. BC. Excavation showed extensive use of mudbrick, stone-paved streets and a well-developed drainage system, and produced ceramic masks of horned animals found both inside and outside buildings, clay seals, querns, pounders, hoes and osteological material. Also named in the 2024 EGQSJ survey.

sites.name_en: Khatis Gora mound and Pshav shrine
sites.description: Late Bronze / Early Iron Age mound settlement on an artificial mound with a surrounding ditch (registry id 24313), Kvemo Kedi community, ~2.5 km north of the park. The registry notes that newly-settled Pshavs have built a prayer niche (salotsavi nishi) on the mound and that this is the origin of its name ('Icon Hill') - a direct, documented link between the transhumant Pshav settler community and an ancient monument. Pottery collected from the surface.

sites.name_en: Early Christian cult building, Kvemo Kedi
sites.description: 5th-6th c. rectangular religious building (registry id 24310), east-west oriented with a west entrance, built of large flat bricks (30 x 30 cm) set in lime mortar on a cobble-reinforced foundation and roofed with red-painted flanged and ridge tiles. Brick altar remains (four to seven courses high) survive on the west, south and north sides over a brick floor; finds include a column base, red-fired antefixes with a relief tree-of-life, iron nails and abundant pottery including red-slipped and glazed faience.

sites.name_en: Burial with Roman helmet, Kvemo Kedi
sites.description: Grave (registry id 24312) that produced a deformed Roman helmet made of thin bronze plates together with a bronze ring fragment, bronze bracelets, red- and brown-fired pottery, drinking cups, bowls, a tray and footed vases. Evidence of Roman-period contact on the Iori plateau north of the park.

6th-5th c. BC metallurgical workshop (registry id 24305) cut into lime-mixed loam and sealed under a 0.7 m redeposited cultural layer of clayey ash and charcoal. Comprises isolated pits and complex rounded, vaulted chambers 0.2-2.3 m deep and 1-2 m across, backfilled after use with production waste, ash and charcoal.

Deserted village site (registry id 24306) with brick and roof-tile scattered over the surface; a test trench exposed brick walls 2.4 m wide bonded with lime mortar and produced glazed and red-fired pottery, building ceramics and a fragment of a cross arm - indicating a Christian medieval settlement abandoned on the Iori plateau.

Second Stone Age open-air station in the Kvemo Kedi area (registry id 24308): an elongated grey flint point of double-ridged triangular section made on a blade with a faceted convex striking platform.

Prehistoric burial ground (registry id 22910) of individual pit graves 0.7-1.5 m deep; the dead were laid mostly contracted, rarely extended, with pottery, ornaments and weapons, and one child was buried on a sherd beside a qvevri. Physical state 'very bad'.
Second burial ground of the Arkhiloskalo group (registry id 22917), dated by its finds to the first half of the 1st millennium BC. The pit graves are badly damaged by ploughing.
Mound settlement near Arkhiloskalo (registry id 22918) dated by pottery to the end of the 2nd and the first half of the 1st millennium BC. Physical state 'bad'.

Settlement group on the Shiraki plain (registry id 23029). One settlement (170 x 70 m) occupies a flat hilltop cut off by a defensive ditch, with a second ditch up to 30 m long running around it; a 13th-15th c. settlement extends over its whole eastern side with dozens of building footprints visible on the surface. A further settlement lies at the end of the ridge towards the Alazani plain.

sites.name_en: Zemo Kedi settlement group (damaged by livestock winter stations)
sites.description: Settlement group north of the park (registry id 23128) explicitly recorded as damaged during the construction of winter stations for livestock - a documented case of transhumant infrastructure destroying archaeology. A circular 100 m settlement adjoins a larger one (300 x 200 m) ringed by a 2 m earthen rampart; a further mound up to 200 m across was completely destroyed in the 1970s, levelled and built over with warehouses.

Roadside shrine niche at Zemo Kedi (registry id 23126, architecture). The present niche was built by local residents in the 1990s on the foundation of a 19th-c. niche; a relief image of St George, probably 9th-10th c., is set into its east wall. Physical state 'satisfactory'. OSM maps a shrine of the same name ~2.6 km east at 41.43310/46.40049.

Soviet-era House of Culture in the Shiraki settler village of Zemo Kedi, recorded as an architectural object in the national registry (id 42636), physical state 'medium'. Registered but unlisted; representative of the surviving Soviet civic infrastructure of the resettled Shiraki villages.

Small ruined church listed as a cultural heritage monument (registry id 6379), recorded under Sighnaghi/Qaragaji but sitting ~90 m from Khornabuji fortress. Built of undressed limestone blocks with lime mortar, deep in the forest south of Khornabuji village; no more than 3.5 m high, about 3 m wide and 4 m long. COORDINATE NOTE: lon 46.136 is outside the 46.2-46.8 sanity window - correct, it is at Khornabuji, NW of the park.

sites.name_en: St Elias the Tishbite church (Elia monastery), Mount Elia
sites.description: Listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 6376) on the crest of Mount Elia, 3 km south of Dedoplistsqaro; APA dates the site to the 5th-7th c. and says the church stands 45-60 m above the base of the limestone rock, reached by a pedestrian trail and stairs. The registry notes nothing survives of the original structures, which may have been entirely contained in a natural cave, larger and habitable at the time; the standing building should be 16th c. An iron cross of the Elia monastery is separately registered at 41.441785/46.108452. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window - correct, ~35 km NW of the park core.

Listed cultural heritage monument (registry id 6375), built 1903-1905 in the Russian colonial settlement of Tsiteli Tsqaro (now Dedoplistsqaro). Cross-domed, 16 m high after reconstruction, built of dressed limestone blocks and red brick with brick openings and facade detailing; interior plastered and whitewashed; physical state 'good'. APA's English pages date it loosely to the 18th c. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window - correct, NW of the park.

Barrow in the Taribana valley west of Dedoplistsqaro (registry id 24284). Under the mound a rounded-corner burial pit 3.3 x 2.2 x 1.2 m, oriented SE-NW, contained 63 human skeletons stacked on one another, aged from 4-5 to 60 years, contracted on the right or left side with heads in varying directions, together with pottery and obsidian. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window - correct, ~40 km NW of the park.

Middle Bronze Age barrow cemetery (registry id 22928) near Dedoplistsqaro - a different place from the Kasristskali village inside the park. Three kurgans were excavated, all robbed; kurgan 2 (stone-and-earth mound 24 x 19 m, 1.2 m high) contained two burial pits, one 2.5 x 3.7 m ringed by large stones with its floor 2.25 m below the fossil humus, plus a 2.1 m-wide robber trench, mixed large pottery fragments and lower-limb bones. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window - correct, NW of the park.

Group of five Late Bronze Age settlements 1-1.5 km apart (registry id 22998), three oval (100-120 m long), a fourth small circular one (20 m) cut off by a defensive ditch, and a fifth on a levelled spot in the eastern part of the mountain commanding both the Didi Shiraki and Patara Shiraki plains. Multi-layer, with Late Bronze, Antique and medieval ceramics; a narrow citadel 60-70 x 25 m with a walled lower settlement 100-150 m long. The name matches the 'village Kaladara' that APA lists for Vashlovani, but this site is ~28 km NW of the park. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window.

Early Iron Age to Hellenistic ritual site (registry id 22886) north of Dedoplistsqaro. A spearhead and a bronze votive war chariot with harnessed horses and rotating wheels were found by chance during works; rescue excavation revealed a round pit filled with pure ash containing the chariot, pottery fragments, a socketed bronze spearhead and a human skull. COORDINATE NOTE: outside the 46.2-46.8 window - correct, ~40 km NW of the park.

sites.name_en: Big Shiraki (Greater Shiraki) abandoned Soviet military airfield
sites.description: Derelict Soviet air base on the Shiraki plain, ~40 km from Dedoplistsqaro and ~3 km north of the Vashlovani NP boundary; Wikidata Q6047327 (46.36733/41.37954), OSM way 74665934 tagged disused:aeroway=aerodrome. Built around 1950; hosted a Guards fighter aviation regiment (sources disagree between the 168th and 178th Guards) that served in the Soviet-Afghan war; the aircraft left for Russia by June 1992, the runways, barracks and ancillary buildings were deserted, the territory was privatised by 2006, and Russian jets bombed the abandoned field on 11 August 2008. Surviving relics mapped nearby: a monument aircraft (41.38854/46.36578), a 'Faceless aviator statue' (41.37374/46.38138) and a vehicle memorial (41.42074/46.37920).

sites.name_en: Big Shiraki hardened aircraft shelter / bunker field
sites.description: Field of 22 mapped military bunkers (OSM ways 1393256413-1393256435, military=bunker) spread between 41.3735-41.3826 N and 46.3722-46.3865 E along the dispersal taxiways of the abandoned Big Shiraki airfield. The coordinate given is one representative bunker; all 22 are individually mapped.

sites.name_en: Former USSR Soviet Army military base ruins (western Shiraki)
sites.name_ka: ყოფილი სსრკ საბჭოთა არმიის ყოფილი სამხედრო ობიექტის ნანგრევები
sites.description: Ruined Soviet Army air-force installation on the Shiraki plain NW of the airfield, mapped as landuse=military / military=base with military_service=air_force and access=yes (OSM way 1193836040). Roughly 5 km north of the park boundary.

sites.name_en: Former USSR military base ruins (eastern Shiraki)
sites.name_ka: ყოფილი სსრკ საბჭოთა არმიის ყოფილი სამხედრო ობიექტის ნანგრევები
sites.description: Second disused Soviet air-force base on the Shiraki plain, ~2 km north of the Vashlovani NP boundary; mapped as brownfield with disused:military=base (OSM way 1219983236, name:en 'Former USSR Military Base').

sites.name_ka: ყოფილი სსრკ საბჭოთა არმიის ყოფილი აეროდრომი
sites.description: Third Soviet air-force site mapped in the Dedoplistsqaro area (OSM way 1222024254, landuse=military / military=base / military_service=air_force), ~9 km north-west of the park. No historical source beyond the OSM record was found.

Georgian Orthodox men's monastery in the Shiraki settler village of Samtatskaro, ~9 km north of the park; mapped in OSM from JumpStart International survey data. The village's St George church is at 41.43195/46.43689 and the Arkhiloskalo Annunciation church at 41.41396/46.43718. Not found in the national immovable-monuments registry, suggesting a modern foundation.

Fort built by Tush highlanders on the Eldar/Shiraki steppe after they were granted grazing rights there in recognition of military service to the kings of Kakheti against Safavid Iran. Wikipedia's Shiraki Plain article states that 'a stone inscription from that period as well as the Eldari fort built by the Tush testifies to their presence in the area'. No coordinate is published in any source consulted and no matching record exists in the national registry (searched 'ელდარ').

Seasonal sheep-driving route between the Tusheti highlands and the Shiraki/Vashlovani winter pastures, crossing the Abano Pass; roughly 200 km / 155 miles, walked in about seven days to Alvani plus a three-day final climb. The Shiraki steppe has been used as Tush winter pasture since the 17th century, when King Levan of Kakheti granted the highlanders winter dwellings and farmland in Shiraki and Alvani; Pshavs, Mtiuls and Kists were employed as hired shepherds. Still practised; the APA map records the resulting shepherd huts inside the park from October to May. No single coordinate applies.

Rock-carved temple decorated with fresco ornament, dated X-XI centuries, which both the Vashlovani and Chachuna APA sightseeing pages place '20 km to the south of Dedoplistskaro Municipality centre, on Iori plateau'. No coordinate is published; the stated bearing and distance would put it on the Iori plateau roughly west-north-west of the park, but nothing was derived because no source gives a point.

APA's Vashlovani sightseeing page lists 'the remains of the 5 thousand years old Kambisena archaeological monument' without location or further detail. Kambisena/Kambechovani is the historical province name for this part of Kakheti, so the entry may refer to the region rather than a discrete site. No registry record (searched 'კამბეჩ', 'კამბისენ') and no coordinate found.

sites.name_en: Shiraki Plain (Didi Shiraki) - winter pasture and Bronze Age settlement landscape
sites.description: Endorheic upland basin of ~300 km2 (study grid 41 18'-41 27' N, 46 11'-46 30' E) immediately north of Vashlovani NP. Forested and continuously inhabited until the end of the 7th c. BC, when settlement abruptly ceased; it carries roughly 100 Late Bronze/Early Iron Age fortified sites of Didnauri and Nazarlebi type, interpreted as evidence of early state formation ~3.2-2.5 ka. From the 17th century onwards it has been the Tush winter pasture, and it remains largely without permanent residential infrastructure beyond livestock farms.

Archaeological site mapped in OSM (way 1049119217, historic=archaeological_site) with the Azerbaijani description 'Alban Kilsəsi Burunqovaq' - a Caucasian Albanian church - immediately south of the Vashlovani/Chachuna boundary across the Iori in Samux rayon, Azerbaijan. Burunqovaq village lies 1.5 km east (41.09399/46.44187, Wikidata Q4908076), with a village cemetery at 41.10333/46.43469. No published excavation or dating was found.

Recorded in Wikidata (Q16374146) as a human settlement inside the Vashlovani bounding box. 'Patara Shiraki' is primarily the name of one of the three plains of the Iori upland (with Didi Shiraki and Zilcha) named in the Didnauri registry record, so this point may label the plain rather than an inhabited or formerly inhabited place. No population data, OSM place node, or heritage record was found for it.

Main river of the Iori plateau (320 km, 4,650 km2 basin, Azerbaijani Qabırlı/Gabirry), which runs along the south-western edge of the park bounding box between roughly lat 41.094-41.149 and lon 46.278-46.424 before entering the Mingachevir reservoir. The official management plan states its water is so heavily abstracted for irrigation that its ecological capacity is entirely exhausted. Coordinate is the midpoint of the OSM river centreline segment lying inside the stated park bbox.

sites.name_en: Alazani River — border reach along the park
sites.description: Forms the park's eastern and southern boundary and the Georgia-Azerbaijan state border (Azerbaijani Qanıx). Mean discharge near Samtatskaro is 75-80 m3/s, making it by far the largest permanent water body of the area; about 20 fish species including wels catfish, carp, pike-perch and Caspian shemaya. Coordinate is the midpoint of the OSM centreline inside the park bbox (mapped extent inside bbox: lat 41.106-41.350, lon 46.640-46.736).

sites.name_en: Alazani open-water polygon at the park's south-east border
sites.description: OSM multipolygon (relation 3755507) delineating the actual wetted channel of the Alazani where it hugs the park boundary — the most directly comparable vector to a Sentinel-2 water mask. Companion channel polygons lie at 41.27083/46.71695, 41.32078/46.68510, 41.36548/46.64350 and 41.07833/46.64026.

The intermittent watercourse that drains the Pantishara badlands, mapped in OSM as one continuous named way tagged intermittent=yes and carrying fords. It is the channel that cuts Pantishara canyon and the Alesilebi razor-ridges; the park's 'Land of the Hidden Water' route exists because its flow is subsurface for most of the year.

Literally 'salt water' — the principal intermittent drainage of the park interior, mapped in OSM as at least nine ways running from about 41.30/46.46 near Kasristskali south-east to about 41.11/46.61 near the Alazani. Consistent with the management plan's statement that many slope streams here are saline; expect only ephemeral standing water in Sentinel-2.

Small slope stream named explicitly in the official management plan as one of the few watercourses of the area; the trekking map labels the valley 'Pl. Goristskaliskhevi' and places two water-source symbols along it. It reaches the Alazani only seasonally.
Small stream/wadi in the south-east of the park draining toward the Alazani floodplain near Takhistskali. Mapped in OSM as waterway=stream; single-source.

Intermittent stream in the far south of the park, crossed by several mapped fords on the track network around 41.104-41.116 / 46.492-46.508. Corresponds to the 'Kumuro' depression named in the management plan's landscape section.

Named in the official management plan as one of the few named slope streams of the area and separately as one of the shrub-covered valleys of the reserve. Flagged on the ground by an interpretive board whose OSM node gives this coordinate (Russian caption 'Соленая вода' = salt water), so the watercourse itself is within a few hundred metres.

Artificial canal taken off the Iori just south of the park bounding box, mapped in OSM as waterway=canal. This is the likeliest candidate for the 'artificial canal off the Iori River' that unverified WWF material describes as feeding solar-pumped gazelle watering holes; treat that linkage as unconfirmed.

Large irrigation canal of the Shiraki/Alazani scheme north of the park, mapped in OSM as waterway=canal with a second segment at 41.50850/46.19452. Coordinate lies just outside the stated sanity box (lat >41.5) — flagged low on that basis only; the feature itself is well mapped.
Named stream on the Shiraki plain north of the park, mapped in OSM. Included as wider Dedoplistsqaro hydrographic context; north-west of the park polygon and at the edge of the sanity box.

Right-bank watercourse on the Azerbaijani side of the Alazani opposite the north-east of the park; a second mapped segment lies at 41.50363/46.83173. Relevant only as cross-border context for Alazani inflows.

The only watercourse of significant size that joins the Alazani anywhere in the project region, according to the official management plan; it flows in from Azerbaijani territory and meets the Alazani exactly on the state border. No published coordinate found in any source consulted.

Named by the management plan as the single most important tributary of the Iori within the protected areas: rises near the Alesilebi by Kvemo Bodbe at 535 m, 29 km long, 395 km2 basin, mean 0.98 m3/s at the mouth but only 0.014 m3/s at low water 10 km down, and the bed normally runs dry. Water is muddy, brackish and undrinkable except at the source. CAUTION: this OSM centreline coordinate is far west of the stated sanity box lon 46.2-46.8, hence low confidence — the river is real and well documented but belongs to the western Dedoplistsqaro / Chachuna side, not the national-park polygon.

Tributary of the Ole, named Mtsaretskali in the management plan (28.8 km2 basin, 12 km). Below its confluence the Ole's channel water progressively disappears, reappearing only in spring and after heavy rain. CAUTION: coordinate lies west of the stated sanity box, hence low confidence on location only; existence documented by both the plan and OSM.
Small river of the Iori system named in the management plan (54 km2 basin, 12 km long) and mapped in OSM. CAUTION: coordinate is west of the stated sanity box, hence low confidence on location only.

Large irrigation reservoir on the Iori, 140,000,000 m3 capacity, operational since 1992, inside Chachuna Managed Reserve roughly 30 km south of Dedoplistsqaro, with Takhti-Tepa mud volcano just to its south. A hydrologist quoted by Georgia Today states it has slowed and effectively blocked the Iori's flow, triggering desertification and the loss of natural downstream flooding — the single most important anthropogenic control on water in this landscape. CAUTION: the Wikidata coordinate (corroborated by the OSM relation centroid 41.29446/45.87779) is well west of the stated sanity box lon 46.2-46.8, so confidence is marked low purely on that basis; existence and position are corroborated by three independent sources.

Small reservoir (OSM way 1105300115, water=reservoir) beside the 'Farmer's House in Vashlovani (Dilicha)' guest house at 41.29427/46.52296. The official trekking map marks a water-source symbol here (derived 41.29434/46.52205, 76 m away), which is the best independent validation of my map georeferencing.

Pair of small reservoirs (OSM ways 1122672871 and 1122672872, the second at 41.28612/46.48183) impounded on the upper Mlashetskali just inside the northern park bbox. Probably stock-watering impoundments; good candidates for seasonal Sentinel-2 water detections.

Two small ponds mapped as water=pond (OSM ways 1321794029 and 1321794030 at 41.29008/46.45921) at the edge of Kasristskali village, with an OSM drinking-water node 30 m away at 41.28959/46.45828. Village-scale artificial water, not natural.

sites.name_en: Ponds near Wiata shelter, central park
sites.description: Pair of small unnamed water polygons (OSM ways 283720410 and 283720411, the second at 41.28139/46.50316) about 2 km south-east of the Wiata shelter node at 41.29950/46.49725, in the Mlashetskali headwater basin. Unnamed in every source consulted.

Isolated unnamed water polygon (OSM way 287061820) in the middle of the park on the Mlashetskali line — one of very few standing-water features in the park interior and therefore a high-value wildlife watering point.

sites.name_en: Seasonal pools in the Pantishara-side wadi
sites.description: Cluster of four small polygons explicitly tagged intermittent=yes, water=stream in OSM (also at 41.21709/46.49785, 41.21476/46.49794 and 41.22002/46.49312) — mapped standing pools in an otherwise dry channel. Exactly the kind of feature that appears and disappears between Sentinel-2 passes.

Salt lake (OSM salt=yes, Wikidata Q24687078; GeoNames classes it LKN 'salt lake' at 41.44104/46.14569, elev 777 m) named in the management plan as one of two salt lakes of the district from which no river originates, and the lake visible eastward from St Elias church on the Eagle Gorge route. An intermittent salt-lake multipolygon is mapped alongside at 41.44088/46.14650. CAUTION: lon 46.148 is west of the stated sanity box, hence low confidence on location only.

The second of the two salt lakes named in the management plan as having no outflowing river; GeoNames records it as 'Ozero Patara-Tba' at 41.46194/46.17798, elev 617 m. CAUTION: lon is west of the stated sanity box, hence low confidence on location only.
Small lake mapped in OSM on the upper Ole system. CAUTION: far west of the stated sanity box; included only to complete the Ole sub-basin picture. Single-source.

The terminal reservoir of both the Iori and the Alazani, in Azerbaijan; it is visible from the Shavi Mta ridge trail inside the park, and the management plan describes the Eldari lowland as tilting toward it. CAUTION: far outside the stated sanity box — included as the regional base level controlling both park rivers.

sites.name_en: Mijniskure well (the park's only reliable drinking water)
sites.description: Well mapped in OSM as man_made=water_well at the Mijniskure ranger station/camp on an Alazani meander. Multiple guides state it is the only reliable drinking-water source inside Vashlovani National Park, with non-potable 'technical' water elsewhere (Vashlovani ranger station, central bungalows). The most important single water point in the park for both visitors and management.
Point mapped in OSM as natural=spring on the northern park approach, about 300 m from Kasristskali village centre and immediately adjacent to the Mlashetskali headwater channel. Single-source.
Point mapped in OSM as natural=spring on the descent from Kasristskali toward the Nagomrebi ridge and the central park, inside the park bounding box. Single-source (OSM).

OSM node tagged natural=spring with an explicit surveyor note: 'Possibly it's a leak of water pipe, or maybe it's kind of intermittent spring. The stream from the source started to flow right I was here', plus a fixme asking for confirmation. Worth targeting specifically — an intermittent spring here would be a genuine find; treat as unconfirmed.
OSM amenity=drinking_water node in Kasristskali, the last settlement on the northern approach; a second, older JumpStart International-sourced node sits at 41.28959/46.45828.

sites.name_en: Drinking-water point on the Alazani terrace near Sabatlo
sites.description: OSM amenity=drinking_water node (JumpStart International survey) on the Alazani terrace in the north-east of the park bounding box, between Sabatlo and the Kaklis Kure floodplain monument.

sites.name_en: Water tower at Vashlovani ranger station / horse ranch
sites.description: OSM man_made=water_tower inside the Vashlovani ranger station compound (camp site at 41.21537/46.43337, plus picnic site, information boards and the Vashlovani Horse Ranch). This is the stored 'technical', non-potable water supply referenced by visitor guides.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-01 (lower Goristskalis Khevi)
sites.description: Blue drinking-water pictogram (glass with droplet) printed on the official Vashlovani Protected Areas trekking map, in the lower Goristskalis Khevi valley in the south-east of the park. Position derived by fitting the map's printed UTM 38N grid; accuracy about ±150 m.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-02 (upper Goristskalis Khevi)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map, upper Goristskalis Khevi, east-central park. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-03 (Imedi / Chighoelta head)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map near the head of the Imedi gorge / Chighoelta Khevi system in the park interior. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-04 (north-east reserve, Zilcha side)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map in the north-east of the protected area, on the ridge system toward Zilcha peak (845 m, OSM 41.26708/46.63738). Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map in the central Mlashetskali basin, close to the mapped OSM pond at 41.25270/46.51943. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-06 (Patara Shiraki / Devil Gorge edge)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the western Patara Shiraki plateau, near Devil Gorge and the Kaladari ridge. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the descent from Kasristskali along the Nagomrebis Tavi ridge toward the central bungalows; it lies about 1.1 km from the OSM spring node at 41.27181/46.44156, which may be the same source. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-08 (north of Pantishara)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the Shiraki edge north of the Pantishara gorge system. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map at or just west of Kasristskali village, the last supply point before entering the park. Derived from the map's UTM grid; note it falls about 0.9 km from the nearest OSM pond, so treat it as a ±200 m search radius.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the western Shiraki steppe along the Dedoplistsqaro approach. CAUTION: lon 46.227 sits at the very edge of the stated sanity box and this point is outside the park polygon. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map at the Dilichi farm; it falls 76 m from the OSM 'Farmer's House in Vashlovani (Dilicha)' node and 155 m from the mapped reservoir there, which validates the georeferencing of the whole WP series.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-12 (western Shiraki, Taribana side)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the western Shiraki/Taribana steppe. CAUTION: near the western edge of the stated sanity box and outside the park polygon. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-13 (Dilichi / Kumuro basin)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map east of Dilichi toward the Kumuro depression. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-14 (eastern Shiraki toward Sabatlo)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the eastern Shiraki plain between the park and Sabatlo village. Derived from the map's UTM grid, accuracy about ±150 m.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the Shiraki plain near Patara-Shiraki settlement (GeoNames 41.29389/46.34083); this was the strongest template match on the sheet. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map beside the gorge labelled 'Gorge Nazariebis Khevi' on the western approach. CAUTION: lon is at/outside the western edge of the stated sanity box and outside the park polygon. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

sites.name_en: Trekking-map water point WP-17 (Alazani terrace near Sabatlo)
sites.description: Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map on the Alazani terrace near Sabatlo, about 1.2 km from the OSM drinking-water node at 41.32206/46.67309 — probably the same supply. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

Drinking-water pictogram on the official park trekking map at Kvemo Kedi village, north of the park on the Shiraki plain. Outside the park polygon but inside the sanity box. Derived from the map's UTM grid.

sites.name_en: Dry-wadi ford cluster on the Mijniskure road
sites.description: OSM maps roughly 40 ford=yes nodes where park tracks cross ephemeral channels; the densest clusters are at 41.10-41.15/46.49-46.51, 41.13-41.15/46.57-46.58, 41.11-41.13/46.64-46.65 and 41.19-41.20/46.51. Each ford is ground truth for a dry wadi and a useful validation set for imagery-detected drainage lines. The coordinate given is one representative crossing on the Mijniskure road.

The wider Pantishara valley, named in the management plan as one of the park's most notable eroded landscapes (clay karst, pillar and tower forms). The park's 'Land of the Hidden Water' route runs through it precisely because water here flows underground rather than at the surface.

Gorge labelled 'Devil Gorge' on the official trekking map below Kaladari Mountain on the western side of the protected area. Coordinate derived from the map label via the printed UTM grid; accuracy about ±300 m. Not present in OSM, GeoNames or Wikidata.

Gorge labelled 'Gorge Nazariebis Khevi' on the official trekking map on the western approach, with a trekking-map water point beside it. Coordinate derived from the map label via the printed UTM grid; lon is at the western edge of the stated sanity box.
Named valley (natural=valley in OSM) on the Alazani side of the park bounding box, between Sabatlo and the Kaklis Kure floodplain. Single-source.

Ravine (GeoNames feature class H, code RVN, id 799092, elevation 617 m) on the Patara Shiraki edge above the Pantishara system. GeoNames coordinates here are rounded to 1/60 degree, so accuracy is roughly ±1 km.
Ravine (GeoNames RVN, id 799094, elevation 459 m) in the park interior below Gora Komroy (41.18333/46.41667); the name matches the Kumra/Kumuro drainage of the southern park.

Ravine (GeoNames RVN, id 799097, elevation 376 m) whose Turkic name means 'salt gorge', consistent with the saline drainage the management plan describes. CAUTION: lon 46.167 is west of the stated sanity box and outside the park; the GeoNames coordinate is rounded, accuracy about ±1 km.

Ranger station, visitor centre/hostel (41.11175/46.64620), bungalows and camping on a meander of the Alazani at the park's southern tip; holds the well that is the only reliable drinking water in the park, and is the designated fly-fishing location. Fords onto the floodplain are mapped at 41.12061/46.64431, 41.12444/46.64899 and 41.12710/46.65099.

Official campsite with picnic site, information map and the trailhead for the Datvis Khevi walk, at the mouth of Bear Gorge in the Pantishara valley. Has no reliable water; visitors are told to carry their own.

Central ranger station and bungalow camp with picnic site, horse ranch and a water tower supplying non-potable 'technical' water; the 900-year-old pistachio tree stands 0.8 km away at 41.20803/46.43603.

Ranger station and camp site on the Bugha Moedani plateau (OSM natural=plateau at 41.13247/46.53878) in the south of the park, with viewpoints over the badlands. Listed by visitor guides as a place with technical water only.

Named locality on the Alazani floodplain terrace in the south-east of the park ('pl. Takhistskali' on the official map); the name literally means 'boar's water', indicating a wildlife watering place. Mapped in OSM as a locality, not as a water feature.
Named Alazani meander bay north of the Kaklis Kure monument, just outside the park bounding box to the north. Part of the same series of floodplain bights as Kaklis Kure and Pshaveliskure.

428 m hill and signed viewpoint over the badlands on the descent to Mijniskure; the management plan names the Usakhelo massif as one of the park's most intensely eroded (denudation) landscapes — water-carved terrain despite the absence of surface water.

9.7 ha natural monument of constantly active mud craters (largest 3.5-4 m across) erupting mud, water, oil and gas at 620 m elevation, immediately south of the Dalis Mta reservoir. A genuine fluid-expulsion feature and so relevant to a water-detection pass, though the surfaces are mud rather than open water. APA's own UTM coordinate (38N X 570695 / Y 4566331) converts to 41.2453/45.84372, agreeing with Wikipedia's 41 14.741 N / 45 50.617 E to within 50 m. CAUTION: lon is far west of the stated sanity box; the site is in the Chachuna/Dali sector, not the national-park polygon.

A second, larger mud-volcano group roughly 22 km west of Takhti-Tepa near the Azerbaijani border, requiring separate Chachuna and border-police permits. I found no coordinate on any page I was able to fetch (a search snippet cited 41.3342/45.7698 from AllTrails, but I could not retrieve that page, so I am not reporting it as a coordinate).

sites.name_en: SABUKO gabion (stone barrage) on the Iori
sites.description: Stone-filled gabion barrage built across the Iori in 2020 by SABUKO to raise water level, restore seasonal flooding of the terraces and lift groundwater; it has restored natural flooding across 3-5 ha of floodplain forest and improved fish habitat, and a second gabion 1.5-1.8 m high has since been prepared. Located in the Chachuna/Iori valley sector; no coordinate is published in any source I could fetch.

sites.name_en: SABUKO livestock watering ponds and well, Chachuna
sites.description: Eight artificial watering ponds plus a well installed by SABUKO in and around Chachuna Managed Reserve so shepherds no longer drive flocks several kilometres daily to water; a companion article counts 10+ water facilities for livestock. These are new, small, artificial water bodies that would appear in recent Sentinel-2 imagery but not on older maps. No coordinates published in any page I could fetch (sabuko.org returned an empty body).

Most of Vashlovani Protected Areas sits within this artesian basin: 4,060 km2, natural fresh groundwater resource 4.5 m3/s, forecast/exploitable resource 3.0 m3/s, per the official management plan citing Georgia's 1991 national resources assessment. This is the subsurface water the park's 'Land of the Hidden Water' route is named for, and it explains springs appearing in otherwise dry gorges. Area feature, no point coordinate.

The management plan states the Alazani plain plays the decisive role in recharging the Alazani artesian basin and holds a large reserve of clean groundwater that is currently not properly exploited. Relevant to the park's eastern, floodplain-fed margin. Area feature, no point coordinate.

The official management plan states that in the first two kilometres of the Ole the river runs between very low, sometimes flooded banks where groundwater emerges and feeds FOUR springs. These are the only springs explicitly enumerated in any Georgian official source for the area, but neither names nor coordinates are given. They should lie within about 2 km downstream of the Ole's source near Kvemo Bodbe (source elevation 535 m), i.e. in the far west of Dedoplistsqaro municipality, outside the national-park polygon.

Viewpoint over the Pantishara Alesilebi — erosion-sculpted pillar and tower badlands formed entirely by water action on clays and sandstones, and the geomorphic signature of the park's flash-flood regime. Named in the management plan as one of the key denudation landscapes.

angle_notes.notes:
RESEARCH ANGLE COVERAGE (official protected-area sources) — what worked and what did not.

BREAKTHROUGH SOURCE: the official Vashlovani Protected Areas Management Plan, approved by Georgian Minister of Environment Order №53 of 2 Aug 2013, full text on matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/1971216 (Georgian). It is the single most authoritative inventory of park infrastructure and zoning and it enumerates exactly:
- EIGHT permanent 24-hour ranger protection stations ("რვა სადღეღამისო მუდმივმოქმედი რეინჯერთა დაცვის სადგური"): ვაშლოვანის (Vashlovani), ცენტრალური შესასვლელის (Central Entrance), ცენტრალური ბუნგალოების (Central Bungalows), მიჯნისყურის (Mijniskure), ვოლიერის (Voliere/gazelle enclosure), შავი მთის (Shavi Mta), კაკლის ყურის (Kaklis Kure), ჰერეთის ფონის (Heretis Foni). Four of these double as park entrances (Vashlovani, Central Entrance, Shavi Mta, Kaklis Kure).
- SEVEN picnic sites: Datvis Khevi, Vashlovani, Central Bungalows, Mijniskure, Takhistskali, Shavi Mta, Kaklis Kure.
- FOUR campsites (20 people each, with fire ring, toilet, bins): Vashlovani, Shavi Mta, Mijniskure, Kaklis Kure.
- SIXTEEN two-person bungalows in three locations: 9 "central bungalows" in Natlistsklis/Lekistskali gorge, 6 in the Mijniskure floodplain, 1 in the Takhistskali floodplain (plan Annex N4).
- THREE viewpoints (Vashlovani built viewpoint, Usakhelo, Shavi Mta), THREE main vehicle roads, SEVEN hiking trails.
- NP ZONING (plan Annex N2): strict nature protection / managed protection / restoration / traditional use / visitor / administrative. The Strict Nature Reserve itself has NO zones. Ranger force in 2013: division head + 2 senior rangers + 23 rangers, 33 staff total.

The official APA Trekking Map PDF (text extracted from the PDF streams) gave all EIGHT numbered tourist routes with roundtrip distances, durations, difficulty and the full visitor rulebook. Route numbering on the map and the trip pages on nationalparks.ge agree.

COVERAGE GAPS on my angle: (1) No salt or mineral spring in or near the park is characterised chemically in any source I could fetch — the springs I report are bare OSM nodes with no water-quality tags, and one is flagged in OSM as possibly a leaking pipe. Halophyte flora on Takhti-Tepa (Kalidium caspicum, Suaeda, Petrosimonia brachiata, Limonium meyeri, per APA) is the only indirect evidence of saline ground. (2) No gypsum or clay outcrop is mapped as a discrete site. The regional gypsum signal is structural, not a visitable outcrop: the Kura fold-thrust-belt detachment lies in Oligocene Maykopian gypsums and clays, and Bukhsianidze & Koiava (2018) describe the Middle Kura Basin as covered by "semi-desert, salt and gypsum steppes". (3) No coordinates are published for the Vashlovani measured stratigraphic section (Forte et al. 2015a, 1475 m thick) — the Sedimentologika PDF discusses it but its section-location table is rendered as figure art; coordinates are presumably in Forte et al. 2015a supplements, which I could not reach. (4) The Chachuna and Dzedzvtakhevi fossil localities are described only by landform name (Akhtakhta-tapa/Akhtatapa, Djighati/Kanly, Pirukugma) and none of those names exist in OSM/Nominatim, so they remain uncoordinated.

USEFUL CROSS-CHECK: the on-site "southern elephant / Mammuthus meridionalis" label at the park's fossil attraction is wrong. Bukhsianidze & Koiava 2018 (Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 63(3):441-461, open access) state the Vashlovani collection contains only Gomphotheriidae indet. and Microstonyx major, fixing the site as late Miocene Turolian MN12 (~7 Ma, Shiraki Formation), not Pleistocene. Travel sources (peakvisor, wander-lush, goingthewholehogg) repeat the elephant/dinosaur/mammoth claim; the park's own signage is the origin of it.

KEY HYDROLOGICAL FACTS FROM THE OFFICIAL MANAGEMENT PLAN (matsne 62824, 2.2.2)
- No river of significant size joins either the Alazani or the Iori inside Dedoplistsqaro municipality. Only small streams come off the flanking slopes — named in the plan as ოლე (Ole), მწარეწყალი (Mtsaretskali), ღორისწყალი (Ghoristskali), ლეკისწყალი (Lekistskali) "and others"; several reach the main rivers only in spring, and many are saline.
- Precipitation 450–520 mm/yr; evaporation 400–430 mm/yr. The plan calls this the driest and most waterless region in Georgia.
- River Ole: rises near Alesilebi by Kvemo Bodbe at 535 m; length 29 km, basin 395 km²; low-flow 0.888 m³/s at the source but only 0.014 m³/s 10 km downstream; mean 0.98 m³/s at the mouth; below the Mtsaretskali confluence the bed usually runs dry, flooding to 1.2 m only in spring/after heavy rain; water is muddy, brackish and undrinkable except at the source. Groundwater in the first 2 km feeds FOUR springs (the plan neither names nor locates them — a real gap).
- River Koda: 54 km² basin, 12 km. River Mtsaretskali: 28.8 km², 12 km.
- Alazani mean discharge near Samtatskaro 75–80 m³/s. Only the Azerbaijani tributary Ajinauri joins in the area, at the state border.
- Most of the protected areas sit on the Iori–Shiraki artesian basin (4,060 km², natural fresh groundwater 4.5 m³/s, exploitable 3.0 m³/s); the Alazani artesian basin holds a large clean groundwater reserve that is currently underused.
- Salt lakes Kochebi and Patara Tba have no outflowing river.
